title: Climate and Gender Indicators Specialist
body:
**Climate and Gender Indicators Specialist**

Africa (multi-country; remote and field-based assignments) | Framework-based consultancy | Subject to contract award and individual assignments

**About Voluntās (Latin: will, goal, purpose, meaning)**

Voluntās was created from the fundamental belief that all human beings have the inherent right to live a meaningful life. **That is why we exist: to realize human potential in all corridors of life** – making every workplace, community, and country on the planet full of hope and dignity. Philosophers by heart and advisors by profession, we use our insights to provide evidence-based inspiration, tools and recommendations for our partners around the world.

Voluntās has established offices in Beirut, Copenhagen, Dakar, Kyiv, Mumbai, Nairobi, Port Sudan, and Tunis. We build on a track record of over 270 projects across Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, serving more than 150 clients. We advise private and public sector actors, including international organizations, government agencies, civil society and foundations, on how to drive meaningful change in societies and organizations.

Our field of expertise is providing fact-based recommendations and policy options grounded in extensive research and data collection in volatile regions and tailored to increase the impact and sustainability of our partners’ efforts.

Voluntās offers a wide range of services across research, policy and governance, including context and thematic analysis, public perception surveys and policy briefs. Under monitoring and social impact, we provide program design, third-party monitoring, evaluations, and social impact measurement. We work across thematic areas including agriculture and food, children and youth, economic development, education, gender, health, migration, governance, media, peace and security, and sustainability.

**About the Role**

Voluntās is preparing a proposal for a multi-year framework covering monitoring, evaluation, reporting and learning (MERL) services for development finance programs in Africa, including agricultural finance, climate resilience and risk financing.

We are seeking an experienced **Climate and Gender Indicators Specialist** to support the design and implementation of climate-sensitive and gender-responsive MERL frameworks, ensuring that climate adaptation, gender equality and inclusion outcomes are effectively measured, monitored and reported across multiple programs and countries.

The framework is anticipated to begin in late 2026 and run for five years. Specific assignments, timelines and levels of effort will be confirmed through individual work orders; appointment and mobilization are not guaranteed.

**Your Responsibilities**

- Develop and harmonize climate adaptation, gender equality and inclusion of indicators within MERL frameworks and theories of change.
- Define indicator reference sheets, baselines, targets and measurement methodologies, including climate resilience metrics and gender-disaggregated indicators.
- Support the application of climate adaptation measurement frameworks and gender-lens investment standards, including the 2X criteria.
- Develop data collection and reporting approaches, including aggregation and attribution rules, to assess climate and gender-related outcomes.
- Support climate and gender analysis across agricultural finance, climate resilience, and risk financing programs.
- Contribute to evaluations, impact assessments, portfolio-level and climate-fund reporting, and knowledge products.
- Provide technical guidance and capacity building to implementing partners on climate-sensitive and gender-responsive MERL.

**Main Competencies**

- Master's degree in environmental sciences, climate change, gender studies, development studies, economics, or related fields.
- **Minimum 7 years of relevant experience integrating both climate adaptation and gender indicators into MERL or results of measurement frameworks.**
- Proven experience designing and applying climate-sensitive and gender-responsive indicators, measurement methodologies, and reporting systems.
- Demonstrated application of climate adaptation and resilience measurement approaches, and familiarity with gender-lens investment standards, including the 2X criteria.
- Strong knowledge of climate resilience, gender equality, women's economic empowerment, and inclusive development.
- Experience supporting multi-country development programs in Africa, preferably in climate adaptation, agricultural finance, or related sectors.
- Strong analytical skills and experience with quantitative and qualitative research, evaluations and results reporting.
- Excellent written and spoken English; French and/or Arabic is an asset.

title: IDC Operations Manager
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**Reports To:** Executive Director  
**Status:** FTE 0.8 - 4 days per week  
**Direct Reports: ●** Finance Coordinator  
● Administration Coordinator  
● Grants and Finance Officer  
**Location:** Remote working, based in **Australia**, **Germany**, **the Netherlands**, or **the United Kingdom**.  
*You must have the right to work in the country for which you apply. IDC is unable to support work visa applications or relocation.*  
**Languages:** Fluency and excellent communication skills in oral and written English  
**Compensation:** Per annum depending on skills and experience:  
**Australia -** SCHADS Level 6, pro rata for 0.8 FTE  
**The Netherlands, Germany, UK -** 48,000-56,000 EUR gross annually for 0.8 FTE (based on a full-time equivalent of 60,000-70,000 EUR)

**Background**

[International Detention Coalition (IDC)](https://idcoalition.org/) is a unique global network of over 200 civil society organisations and individuals in more than 75 countries, which coordinates with members and partners on advocacy, research, coalition and capacity building, to eliminate immigration detention and advance rights-based alternatives to detention. IDC is a highly recognised, impact-driven organisation, offering a stimulating workplace committed to local, national, regional and global change.

**Role Purpose**

The Operations Manager is responsible for making sure the organisation has the financial, legal, human resources (HR) systems, and operational infrastructure needed to function effectively, and sustainably, including risk management and ensuring compliance in the countries where IDC operates.

**Role Summary**

The Operations Manager provides strategic leadership for the organisation's financial, legal, HR systems, and operational infrastructure, ensuring that the organisation has the systems, capacity and controls required to operate effectively, sustainably and compliantly in multi-currency and multi-country settings.

The role sets the frameworks, standards and priorities through which operational functions are delivered, providing oversight of the Finance Coordinator, Administration Coordinator and Grants and Finance Officer, as well as relevant external providers. The Operations Manager focuses on organisational systems, planning, risk, quality and improvement.

The role is responsible for strengthening the organisation's operational infrastructure as it develops, ensuring that systems are fit for purpose, risks are identified and appropriately managed, legal and regulatory obligations are met, and personnel have the systems and support they need to work effectively.

The Operations Manager reports to the Executive Director (ED) and works closely with the Programmes Manager, Finance and Administration personnel, Regional Managers, and relevant service providers. The Operations Manager forms part of the Senior Management Team.

**Role Responsibilities**

**Finance and Organisational Sustainability**

- Provide strategic oversight of financial management, grants financial management, budgeting, forecasting and organisational finances.
- Oversee and support the Finance Coordinator and Grants and Finance Officer, ensuring effective implementation of finance and grants systems.
- Work closely with the ED, Programmes Manager, finance and admin team, and relevant managers on annual budgeting and financial planning.
- Ensure effective monitoring of financial performance, cash flow, expenditure and financial risks, providing advice to the ED and Senior Management Team.
- Oversee the establishment and management of appropriate financial controls, payrolls systems, approval processes and delegations.
- Oversee relationships with accountants, auditors, tax advisers and other financial service providers.
- Lead on the improvements to financial systems as the organisation develops or operates in new places.
- Oversee budgeting systems and allocations ensuring accurate compliance of grants finance and audit requirements.
- Work closely with the Finance Coordinator and oversee the annual audit processes for IDC and other related programme audits.
- Ensure financial systems provide accurate and timely information for informed organisational decision-making.

**Human Resources Systems**

- Support the Executive Director to implement the organisation's human resources systems, ensuring personnel structures and capabilities are aligned with organisational priorities and needs.
- Develop and implement recruitment and planning strategies and systems, including approaches to attracting, retaining and developing personnel across different regions and jurisdictions.
- Develop appropriate and coherent benchmarks and frameworks for personnel roles that are localised, including remuneration, benefits and capacity, and use these to inform organisational planning, monitoring and recruitment.
- Oversee and manage human resources systems, including employment arrangements in different jurisdictions, benefits, onboarding, performance management and other HR related systems.
- Ensure human resources practices are compliant with applicable local legislation and organisational policies.
- Support the enhancement of a wellbeing culture at IDC with related systems and benefits.
- Oversee and support the Administration Coordinator's implementation of HR processes, ensuring systems are consistent, effective and fit for purpose.

**Risk, Compliance and Contracts**

- Work closely with the ED to coordinate the organisational risk management framework, including the development, monitoring and mitigation of key organisational risks.
- Manage and provide oversight of the organisation's legal entities and ensure statutory, regulatory and governance obligations are met as needed.
- Establish and maintain appropriate internal controls across financial, operational, HR, data and compliance functions.
- Oversee the organisation's grant finance compliance infrastructure, working closely with the ED, Programmes Manager and Grants and Finance Officer.
- Ensure systems are in place to monitor donor financial and administrative requirements, contractual obligations, reporting deadlines and compliance risks.
- Oversee organisational contracts and agreements, ensuring appropriate systems for review, approval, documentation and record-keeping.
- Coordinate legal, tax and compliance advice where required.
- Ensure appropriate continuity, sustainability and contingency planning is in place.

**Policies, Systems and Administration**

- Lead the development, review and implementation of organisational policies, procedures and operational frameworks, liaising with the Executive Director.
- Ensure organisational processes, approval pathways and delegated authorities are clear, proportionate and consistently applied.
- Provide strategic oversight of IT, cybersecurity, data protection and digital infrastructure.
- Ensure appropriate systems, security arrangements and technology standards are in place for a global remote organisation.
- Oversee organisational procurement frameworks and controls.
- Provide oversight and support to the Administration Coordinator, ensuring administrative systems are efficient and responsive to organisational needs.
- Identify opportunities to streamline processes, improve systems and reduce unnecessary administrative burden.

**Organisational Development & Operational Improvement**

- Lead the ongoing development of the organisation's operational infrastructure and systems, as its size, funding and geographic reach evolve.
- Regularly and proactively assess organisational systems, platforms, capacity and processes to identify gaps, risks and opportunities for improvement.
- Develop practical frameworks and standards to strengthen organisational effectiveness, accountability and resilience.
- Lead operational improvement and organisational development initiatives and monitor their implementation.
- Identify emerging organisational needs and advise the ED on appropriate systems, structures and resourcing.
- Any other relevant tasks agreed with the Executive Director.

**Core Responsibilities**

- Actively contribute to a culture of agile learning, collaboration, teamwork and support within IDC’s team.
- Demonstrate passion and alignment with IDC’s mission, vision and core values of innovation, collaboration, respect, inclusion, representation and being solutions-focused.
- Demonstrate an understanding of IDC policies to ensure a positive and safe working environment for all.
- Actively engage with organisational systems, processes and infrastructure to ensure sustainability and appropriate safeguarding of institutional knowledge, assets and core activities over time.

**Key Selection Criteria**

**Essential Criteria**

- Relevant tertiary qualification and/or equivalent professional experience in business administration, finance, human resources, organisational management, non-profit management or a related field.
- Significant experience in operations, organisational management, finance and/or administration within a non-profit, social impact or other complex organisation.
- Demonstrated experience managing and supporting personnel responsible for finance, HR, administration or other operational functions.
- Strong understanding of organisational financial management, including budgeting, forecasting, financial controls and financial risk.
- Experience overseeing HR and employment processes, ideally across multiple jurisdictions or employment arrangements.
- Experience managing organisational compliance and/or legal or regulatory requirements.
- Demonstrated ability to develop, implement and improve organisational systems, policies and processes.
- Experience working in a geographically distributed or remote organisation or demonstrated ability to manage operational functions across locations.
- Strong judgement, problem-solving and prioritisation skills, with the ability to balance strategic priorities with responsive day-to-day operational needs.
- A high level of flexibility and adaptability, including the ability to work well and collaboratively with others.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and practically regarding complex matters.
- High level of integrity, discretion and attention to detail, with the ability to handle sensitive financial, personnel and organisational matters.

**Desirable Criteria**

- Experience operating across multiple jurisdictions
- Experience with grant management and donor compliance
- Experience with HR, finance, IT or other organisational systems and technology.
- Experience in a human rights, migration, social justice or other values-driven organisation.

title: Liberia-Based Sectoral and Technical Experts and Trainers
body:
**Position:** Sectoral Technical Experts / Trainers - Liberia  
**Type:** Consultancy / Project-based / Roster  
**Location:** Liberia  
**Organization:** STOOS Consulting

**STOOS Consulting** is inviting qualified **sectoral technical experts, trainers, facilitators, researchers, and consultants in Liberia** to join its roster for upcoming humanitarian, development, research, assessment, capacity building, monitoring, evaluation, and third-party monitoring opportunities across the country.

This call is open to experienced professionals from different technical backgrounds who are interested in supporting future assignments with **UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs, donors, development partners, local organizations, and community-based actors**.

**About STOOS Consulting**

**STOOS Consulting** is an international consulting firm specialized in **Third-Party Monitoring, MEAL, research and assessments, evaluations, data collection, capacity building, conflict and gender analysis, market systems research, and economic empowerment studies**. STOOS works in complex humanitarian and development contexts to produce practical, field-based, and evidence-driven findings that support programme quality, accountability, learning, and decision-making.

Through its network of national and international experts, STOOS supports assignments in areas such as **needs assessments, baseline and endline studies, final evaluations, outcome monitoring, technical training, capacity building, qualitative and quantitative research, community consultations, and field monitoring**.

**Profile of Experts Sought**

STOOS is looking to expand its Liberia roster with qualified experts and trainers in a wide range of sectors, including but not limited to **WASH, health, nutrition, protection, GBV, child protection, education, food security and livelihoods, climate resilience, disaster risk reduction, shelter, social protection, TVET, economic empowerment, migration, gender, disability inclusion, peacebuilding, conflict sensitivity, and MEAL**.

STOOS also welcomes applications from experts with experience in **research design, qualitative and quantitative data collection, training facilitation, curriculum development, institutional capacity building, market assessments, youth employment, entrepreneurship, community engagement, safeguarding, accountability to affected populations, and humanitarian/development programme quality**.

**Main Areas of Work**

Selected experts may be contacted for future assignments involving **technical training, capacity building, sectoral assessments, programme evaluations, field research, tool development, data collection supervision, contextual analysis, report writing, quality assurance, and technical advisory support**.

Depending on the opportunity, experts may support **KIIs, FGDs, surveys, community consultations, workshops, technical reviews, training delivery, data analysis, and preparation of practical recommendations** tailored to the Liberia context.

**Liberia Context and Relevant Experience**

Candidates with strong knowledge of Liberia's humanitarian and development context are encouraged to apply, especially those with experience related to **public health, WASH, education, food security and livelihoods, nutrition, climate resilience, disaster risk reduction, environmental and natural resource governance, social protection, gender equality, disability inclusion, youth employment, economic empowerment, migration, and community resilience**.

Experience working with communities in **urban, rural, forested, coastal, border, or hard-to-reach areas** is highly valued. STOOS particularly welcomes experts who can work respectfully with **women, youth, children, persons with disabilities, rural communities, returnees, migrants, farmers, fisherfolk, low-income households, and other vulnerable groups**.

**Key Skills and Qualifications**

Candidates should have relevant professional experience in one or more technical sectors and a strong understanding of the **Liberia context**, including local institutions, community structures, civil society actors, government partners, access dynamics, and humanitarian/development priorities.

Applicants are encouraged to apply if they have worked with **UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs, local organizations, government partners, donor-funded programmes, academic institutions, consulting firms, or community-based initiatives**.

Strong candidates will demonstrate practical experience in **training, facilitation, technical advisory work, assessments, monitoring and evaluation, field research, community engagement, or programme implementation**.

Knowledge of **Do No Harm, safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, gender sensitivity, disability inclusion, ethical research, confidentiality, conflict sensitivity, and accountability to affected populations** is highly desirable.

Experience using digital tools such as **KoboToolbox, ODK, SurveyCTO, Excel, SPSS, Power BI, NVivo, or similar platforms** is considered an asset, depending on the assignment.

**Language Skills**

Fluency in **English** is required for most field-based and community-level assignments.

Strong **written English** is preferred, especially for assignments involving technical reports, donor documentation, training materials, data analysis, and communication with international teams.

Knowledge of local languages such as **Liberian English, Kpelle, Bassa, Dan/Gio, Mano, Kru, Grebo, Loma, Mandingo, Vai, Gola, Kissi, or other local languages** is a strong advantage, especially for assignments in specific counties, remote or forested areas, coastal communities, or border areas.

Knowledge of **Do No Harm, safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, gender sensitivity, disability inclusion, ethical research, confidentiality, conflict sensitivity, and accountability to affected populations** is highly desirable.

Experience using digital tools such as **KoboToolbox, ODK, SurveyCTO, Excel, SPSS, Power BI, NVivo, or similar platforms** is considered an asset, depending on the assignment.

**Language Skills**

Fluency in **Burmese (Myanmar language)** is required for most field-based and community-level assignments.

Good working knowledge of **English** is strongly preferred, especially for assignments involving technical reports, donor documentation, training materials, data analysis, and communication with international teams.

Knowledge of local languages such as **Shan, Karen, Kachin, Chin, Mon, Rakhine, Kayah/Karenni, Wa, or other ethnic languages** is a strong advantage, especially for assignments in specific states and regions, border areas, conflict-affected areas, or ethnic minority communities.

title: General coordinator (head of mission) (F/M) - Pakistan
body:
For more than 40 years, Médecins du Monde (MdM), a campaigning medical organisation committed to international solidarity, has been caring for the most vulnerable populations here and abroad. It has continued to bear witness to obstacles that exist in accessing healthcare and has secured sustainable improvements in health-for-all policies.

Those working for this independent organisation do not solely dispense care and treatment but condemn violations of human dignity and rights and fight to improve matters for populations living in precarious situations.

MdM France currently works in 30 countries across all continents to facilitate access to healthcare through 6 political battles:

- Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights
- Migration, Exile, Human Rights and Health
- Harm Reduction
- Environment and Health
- Humanitarian Space
- Healthcare systems and rights

**MdM in Pakistan**

MdM France has been operating in Pakistan since 1996, mainly in Punjab and KPK provinces. In Punjab, over the past 30 years, MdM has been implementing Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) including family planning and gender based violence projects. Present since 2009 in KP, MdM has been working with the Afghan refugees and internally displaced persons providing essential primary healthcare services including mental health and psychological support. In KP, across the course of the years, we have covered many districts and have built strong acceptance among the local communities and authorities. We have also responded to multiples emergencies including the 2022 and 2025 floods.

For the 2027–2029 period, MdM will continue to focus on advancing on SRHR as the central pillar of all programming in Pakistan. All interventions will be firmly grounded in a comprehensive, integrated, and rights-based SRHR strategy with particular focus on access to family planning services and cervical cancer awareness and screening. Developing specific initiatives focused on cervical cancer would be critical to the mission. Additionally, MdM is monitoring the situation related to humanitarian needs of Afghan refugees in KP and will intend to develop new actions to ensure humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable.

Currently the mission has a portfolio of around 500K€/year, with 20 staffs and 2 offices (coordination in Islamabad and one field office in Mardan/KP). A variety of institutional donors used to support the mission, but the funding environment is currently shrinking, and MdM is covering the mission with core funds. One of the main stakes of 2027 will be to secure new institutional fundings and ensure sustainability of MdM in the country.

**About the role**

As general coordinator, you will supervise the proper implementation of MdM strategy and operations in the country.

One of your main responsibilities is to drive a strategic restructuring of the Pakistan mission, ensuring the transition to a strengthened and autonomous national team.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the desk manager, you are responsible for the overall management of the Pakistan mission.

Your main responsibilities are the following:

- Recruit, manage, train and motivate the mission’s team
- Define the operational and advocacy strategy together with the coordination team, the desk manager and the volunteer board delegates of the mission
- Plan and monitor activities, implement corrective action when necessary, providing technical support to the team
- Represent MdM with authorities, local actors, partners, donors and the media
- Monitor partnership agreements with partners, authorities and donors, seek out and develop new partnerships, and ensure or supervise fundraising
- Ensure the financial coverage of the mission by leading fundraising and budget management
- Draft, adapt and monitor safety regulations and procedures and coordinate crisis management in the region
- Implement and monitor the application of MdM’s programmatic and support services framework, policies and procedures
- Supervise reporting to MdM and donors

**Who you’ll work with**

You will report directly to the Desk Manager based at HQ.

As General Coordinator, you will be the head of the country coordination team and you will manage directly a team composed of: Deputy Coordinator programs, Deputy Coordinator in charge of support services, Medical Advisor, Humanitarian Access and Risks Advisor and Field Coordinator/KP.

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you:**

- Have 5+ years' experience in the humanitarian sector, including coordination and expatriate roles
- Have led teams and operations in complex or insecure environments
- Are confident representing an organisation with donors, authorities and humanitarian actors
- Can negotiate effectively, manage risks and oversee security matters
- Bring strong strategic thinking and sound operational judgment
- Have experience with programme, budget and support function management, ideally in health and SRHR
- Enjoy coaching teams, building capacity and developing talent
- Communicate with diplomacy, adapt quickly and lead through uncertainty
- Are comfortable with Microsoft Office and mapping tools
- Are fluent in English

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Prefer stable environments with limited operational or security challenges
- Are uncomfortable making difficult decisions, negotiating or representing an organisation externally
- Prefer specialist or technical roles over broad leadership and management responsibilities
- Are not aligned with MdM’s values

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS**

Contract & status:

- Gross monthly salary: 3 664 €
- Fixed-term contract of 6 months starting on January 2027
- Single posting

Work environment:

- Position based in Islamabad with frequent travels to field locations (office in Mardan/KP)

Benefits:

- 13th month salary (paid in 2 installments after 6 months of service)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Individual guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

Essentials:

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

title: Monitoring Officer - Roster
body:
**Monitoring Officer - Roster**

**Summary**

**Languages:** One of 12 roster languages (Pashto, Dari, Levantine Arabic, Sudanese Arabic, Bengali, Egyptian Arabic, Urdu, Moroccan Darija, Iraqi Arabic, Kurdish Sorani, Kurdish Badini and Somali), plus English and/or Arabic and/or French.

**Role:** Structured monitoring phone calls with a sample of people who received support from our counsellors.

**Based:** Remote, from anywhere.

**Roster:** Unpaid standby pool from January 2027 to May 2029. Joining is not a job offer.

**Reports to:** M&E Lead.

**Contract:** Consultancy contract per campaign.

## **Why this roster**

New Pathways to Resilience (NPR) is a three-year project funded by the EU’s Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF). It is built around Seefar’s Crisis Adaptation Mechanism (CAM), which lets the project respond when migration patterns shift. When a monitored indicator crosses its threshold, a campaign may be activated for a new audience or language, and Seefar then has two weeks to launch it. That is too short to recruit from scratch, so we keep an unpaid standby pool of vetted Counsellors, Social Media Officers and Monitoring Officers for 12 languages, ready to be contracted the moment a campaign is approved.

## **Who we are**

Seefar Foundation is a social enterprise with a simple mission: to transform the lives of vulnerable people. Through programmes rooted in technology, psychology and behaviour change, we help people build the skills and confidence they need to make a positive contribution to their communities. It’s how we support governments in finding solutions to challenges around irregular migration, poverty, human trafficking, violent extremism, access to justice, and more.

Our exceptional team of over 100 consultants are problem solvers and innovators, delivering programmes and high impact research. Together, we solve difficult, high impact problems for governments and NGOs across communications, digital, and research, monitoring and evaluation in Africa, Asia, and Europe.

## **Your Responsibilities**

1. Checkback calls (80%). Take part in a paid introductory training session and get to know the campaign, the checkback tools and the ethical guidelines for engaging with vulnerable people. Then conduct structured checkback calls by phone with a sample of people who received support from our counsellors at 3 weeks, 3 months or 12 months after their one-to-one support session with a Seefar counsellor. Administer the standardised checkback tools (Kobo forms) consistently on every call, capturing quantitative and qualitative data on wellbeing, migration decisions, referrals and satisfaction with the support received. Submit completed records within 24 hours of each call.
2. Data quality and learning (15%). Share observations on patterns in responses, data quality issues and anything that may affect the reliability of findings. Support translation or back-translation of M&E tools and templates between your language and English when needed. Manage your own call schedule and flag promptly when participants cannot be reached.
3. Independence and safeguarding (5%). Because checkbacks are a quality control process, stay independent of the counsellors and Social Media Officers delivering the campaign, so that outcome data remains neutral and credible. Treat all participant data with strict confidentiality in line with Seefar’s data protection standards, and escalate safeguarding concerns immediately.

## **Who you are**

**To succeed, you’ll need:**

- At least 3 years’ experience in monitoring and evaluation, data collection or a related field.
- Experience conducting structured telephone or remote surveys or interviews.
- Fluency in at least one roster language, and working proficiency in written and spoken English and/or Arabic and/or French.
- Computer literacy and a reliable internet connection.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills, and the ability to engage sensitively with vulnerable people.
- The ability to work independently and remotely, and manage your own workload against deadlines.
- Strong attention to detail and organisational skills.
- A private, quiet space for confidential calls.
- The ability to work as an independent consultant and receive payments in EUR by international bank transfer.

You should meet all of the above. It’s a bonus if you have experience on humanitarian, development or migration-related programmes, familiarity with psychosocial support or returnee contexts, or experience using Kobo Toolbox or similar platforms.

## **How you work**

**Spoken/Written English and/or French and/or Arabic**

You write clear notes and observations in English and/or French and/or Arabic that others can act on.

**Roster language**

You interview fluently in one of these 12 languages: Pashto, Dari, Levantine Arabic, Sudanese Arabic, Bengali, Egyptian Arabic, Urdu, Moroccan Darija, Iraqi Arabic, Kurdish Sorani, Kurdish Badini, Somali.

**Structured interviewing**

You follow a questionnaire consistently, without sounding scripted.

**Sensitivity**

You put people at ease, recognise distress and respond with care.

**Data accuracy**

The data you collect is complete, consistent and entered within 24 hours.

**Independence**

You keep a clear boundary from the delivery team so data stays credible.

**Translation**

You translate and back-translate M&E tools accurately.

**Digital skills**

You are comfortable with Kobo or similar tools and Google Suite.

**Self regulation**

You respond constructively to professional and emotional challenges.

## **How the roster works**

- **It is not a job offer.** Joining the roster does not guarantee work, and you can work elsewhere in the meantime.
- **Everyone in the pool counts as equally qualified.** When a campaign is activated, we pick the best match on language, gender, location and availability. The reason for every choice is recorded.
- **When a campaign is approved,** we contact Monitoring Officers about six weeks before starting.
- **Quarterly check-ins.** Every three months we ask whether you want to stay, pause or leave, and whether you could start within your notice period. Missing one check-in makes your place dormant; missing two in a row means it expires and your data is deleted.
- **You remain on the roster** until you choose to leave, miss two check-ins in a row, or NPR ends in May 2029.

### **What we offer**

- Paid training once you are hired.
- Freedom to work elsewhere while on the roster, and to decline an offer without penalty.
- Work from anywhere, and return to the pool or apply for other Seefar roles after a campaign.
- Only months worked on an activated campaign are paid.

### **Who you’ll work with**

You will report to NPR’s M&E Lead. To keep outcome data neutral, you will work independently of the counsellors and Social Media Officers delivering the campaign, while sharing what you learn with the M&E team. You will join a team with a mix of perspectives, backgrounds, technical expertise and lived experience, working across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia.

Assess each person’s psychological distress and mental health needs, and respond appropriately, for example with empathetic listening, coping strategies, or grief and loss support.

Follow up with individuals to match them with a suitable referral and accompany them through the process, including emotional, medical, livelihood and other support services where available. 3. Records, safeguarding and teamwork (10%). Keep timely, confidential records of every session. Flag safeguarding concerns immediately. Take part in paid training before consultations start, attend team meetings, recommend ways to improve the service, and stay reachable to your supervisor during working hours.

## **Who you are**

**To succeed, you’ll need:**

- At least 2 years’ professional experience as a counsellor or in a similar role.
- Experience delivering remote counselling and trauma-informed care.
- Fluency in English and/or Arabic and/or French and in at least one roster language.
- Demonstrated experience working with vulnerable people, and a thorough understanding of confidentiality.
- Experience working remotely across platforms such as Google Suite, and a reliable internet connection.
- A private, quiet space for confidential calls.
- The ability to work as an independent consultant and receive payments in EUR by international bank transfer.

You should meet all of the above. It’s a bonus if you have:

- A BA degree in Counselling, Social Work, Psychology or another mental health-related field.
- Knowledge of legal migration pathways relevant to your audience.
- Experience working with migrants from or in your audience’s countries.
- Experience counselling people experiencing crisis, loss, grief, suicidal ideation, depression or anxiety.

Women counsellors are especially needed for the Somali-speaking pool.

## **How you work**

**Spoken/Written English and/or French and/or Arabic**

You write clear notes and observations in English and/or French and/or Arabic that others can act on.

**Roster language**

You counsel fluently in one of these 12 languages: Pashto, Dari, Levantine Arabic, Sudanese Arabic, Bengali, Egyptian Arabic, Urdu, Moroccan Darija, Iraqi Arabic, Kurdish Sorani, Kurdish Badini, Somali.

**Empathy**

You stay calm, patient and present with people in distress.

**Assessment**

You recognise distress and mental health needs, and respond appropriately.

**Information**

You explain migration risks and safe, legal alternatives without judgement.

**Confidentiality**

You protect participants’ data and know when to raise safeguarding concerns.

**Record keeping**

You document every session on time, every time.

**Digital skills**

You are comfortable with using a laptop or phone and Google Suite.

**Self regulation**

You respond constructively to professional and emotional challenges.

## **How the roster works**

- **It is not a job offer.** Joining the roster does not guarantee work, and you can work elsewhere in the meantime.
- **Everyone in the pool counts as equally qualified.** When a campaign is activated, we pick the best match on language, gender, location and availability. The reason for every choice is recorded.
- **When a campaign is approved,** we contact counsellors about three weeks before starting.
- **Quarterly check-ins.** Every three months we ask whether you want to stay, pause or leave, and whether you could start within your notice period. Missing one check-in makes your place dormant; missing two in a row means it expires and your data is deleted.
- **You remain on the roster** until you choose to leave, miss two check-ins in a row, or NPR ends in May 2029.

### **What we offer**

- Paid training once you are hired.
- Freedom to work elsewhere while on the roster, and to decline an offer without penalty.
- Work from anywhere, and return to the pool or apply for other Seefar roles after a campaign.
- Only months worked on an activated campaign are paid.

### **Who you’ll work with**

You will report to the Project Coordinator, or to a team leader on larger campaigns, and work alongside other counsellors. The Social Media Officer’s campaign brings people to you, and Monitoring Officers later check back, independently, with a sample of the people you counselled. You will join a team with a mix of perspectives, backgrounds, technical expertise and lived experience, working across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia.

title: Assistant.e Qualité et Administratif - Projet Antibiogo F/H
body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

Sous la supervision de l’équipe de Coordination du projet et en collaboration étroite avec l’équipe QARA, elle/il est chargé du suivi administratif des ressources du projet (RH, comptable, budgétaire), de la partie approvisionnement du projet et participera activement à la mise en œuvre de la procédure de gestion documentaire selon la norme ISO 13485 auprès de l’ensemble des équipes (Clinique, Développement/Produit, QARA et Coordination).

**Principales responsabilités :**

**1. Suivi Administratif des Ressources du projet**

**a. Gestion des Ressources humaines**

- Collecter et enregistrer les données des collaborateurs pour la constitution et le suivi des dossiers RH.
- Collaborer avec le département RH de MSF Asso pour la rédaction et la saisie des contrats conformément au droit du travail français et du Système d’Information RH de MSF.
- Organiser l’arrivée des nouveaux collaborateurs : matériel, badges, briefings, intégration administrative et opérationnelle.
- Maintenir à jour les tableaux de suivi des contrats du personnel (employés et consultants).
- Planifier les entretiens annuels.
- Diffuser le planning des déplacements/ absences/ occupation des bureaux et animer son utilisation par les équipes
- Mettre en forme et diffuser les annonces de recrutement selon la stratégie définie
- En conformité avec la procédure RH du QMS, maintenir à jour la documentation et le reporting RH (organigramme, tableau de bord des formations, descriptifs de postes, et autres enregistrements RH) nécessaire au suivi des indicateurs de performance.

**b. Gestion comptable et budgétaire du projet**

- Participer à la construction du budget et au suivi de son exécution avec le responsable du projet.
- Contribuer à la préparation des reportings financiers et narratifs à destination des bailleurs.
- Assurer le suivi des dépenses et de la refacturation en lien avec la comptabilité et le contrôle de gestion de MSF Asso et de la Fondation MSF
- Vérifier et transmettre les notes de frais des employés à la comptabilité.

**2. Approvisionnement**

- Coordonner les commandes et livraisons en fonction des besoins du projet.
- Réaliser les demandes d’achat dans le Système d’Information Finance/Achat de MSF et suivre les réceptions des prestations conformément à la Procédure Achat/Fournisseurs
- En conformité avec la procédure Achat/Fournisseur du QMS, maintenir à jour la documentation et le reporting Supply (tableau de suivi des fournisseurs, audits et évaluations des fournisseurs, et autres enregistrements supply) nécessaire au suivi des indicateurs de performance.
- Participer à la sélection des fournisseurs.

**3. Gestion documentaire du projet (ISO 13485)**

- Participer au pilotage opérationnel (organisation et mise en œuvre) de la procédure de gestion documentaire, en garantissant le maintien, la mise à jour, l’accessibilité et l’archivage de la documentation du projet (procédures, ‘template’, enregistrements) conformément aux exigences de la norme et de la procédure.
- Assurer un soutien méthodologique aux équipes pour le formatage des documents.
- Veiller à la bonne mise en forme et à la standardisation des documents.
- Suivre la réalisation des actions, la résolution des problèmes liés à la procédure de gestion documentaire.
- Participer au prochain déploiement d’un outil de GED (gestion électronique des documents) : organisation de la migration des documents, formation des utilisateurs et support à la prise en main.

**4. Appui à la coordination de projet**

- Assurer le suivi et l’animation des dossiers ou projets spécifiques qui lui sont confiés (support à la gestion de l’information et aux activités de plaidoyer).
- Apporter son soutien à l'organisation des réunions et veiller au suivi des plans d'action correspondants
- Rédiger les comptes rendus des comités de pilotage, réunions d’équipe.
- Soutenir le bon fonctionnement des activités transverses du projet selon les besoins.

**Profil recherché :**

**Formation**

- Formation Bac+2 minimum en gestion, administration ou qualité essentielle

**Expérience professionnelle**

**Rémunération et avantages :** 41,1 K€ brut annuel sur 13 mois. 22 jours de RTT par an. Télétravail selon les règles en vigueur chez MSF (2 j/sem.). Mutuelle prise en charge à 100%. Titres-restaurant de 12€ (prise en charge à 60% par MSF). Prise en charge à 50% de l'abonnement de transport en commun (hebdomadaire, mensuel ou annuel) ou indemnité kilométrique vélo (0,25€ par km, limité à 450€ par an).

title: Terre des Hommes - External Evaluation of Decentralized Organizational Model
body:
## 1.Presentation of Terre des hommes

As he leading Swiss organization for children’s rights, created in 1960, the Terre des hommes foundation is committed to protecting children’s lives and their rights, and improving their well-being. We aim to do so through innovative programmes focused on health, migration and access to justice, specially designed to have both short- and long-term impacts.

For more than 60 years, we have been working in difficult situations, in countries at war, regions devastated by natural disasters, and places where poverty and malnutrition force millions of children and their families to migrate elsewhere. We provide direct and indirect support to millions of children, their families and communities in around thirty countries every year, in close cooperation with our local partners. [www.tdh.org](http://www.tdh.org)

## 2.Context

The Terre des hommes Decentralization Project (hereinafter ‘the Project’) is an organizational transformation project consistent with the evolution of the international development sector.

The objective is to identify, build and implement a decentralized organizational model that empowers regions and countries and converts its headquarters in Switzerland into a centre of expertise.

More specifically, the objectives of the Project are based on the following items:

- **Proximity** to the field, improved context-specific knowledge, meaningful regional projects and consortia, and an improved response to children's needs.
- **Influence & advocacy** in relation to regional policies of interest to Tdh, initiate and contribute to regional advocacy.
- **Positioning & visibility** towards the regional aid and coordination agencies, recognition as a key organization in the field of children's rights, and authority based on our expertise.
- Integration of **local expertise** into regional offices as much as possible.
- Increased institutional **fundraising**, influence of donor strategies, strong relationships with key donors.
- **Efficiency** through optimized functions, processes, with strong reliance on local expertise.

The Project began in 2022, with a planned completion by the end of 2025; the roll out of the third and last Regional setup was delayed because of the reexamination of its modalities and reporting lines especially, and the new organizational model will be fully operational at the end of 2026.

Terre des hommes is now undertaking an external evaluation to assess the relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, and fitness for purpose of the decentralized model in relation to its mission, strategy, and operating context.

Consistent with [OECD/DAC Evaluation Criteria](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2019/12/better-criteria-for-better-evaluation_f7a307eb/15a9c26b-en.pdf), the evaluation is commissioned at a time of governance review, with the intention of informing decision‑making by senior management and the governing body. The evaluation will allow for significant developments in the global development sector in 2025 and 2026, that is, after its design and roll-out.

### Monitoring

Under the sponsorship of the Director General, the **Project Steering Committee** the Directors of Operations and his Deputy, People & Culture, Finance & Logistics, Resource Mobilization & Communication, Digital, Innovation and ICT, and the Chief of Staff.

An initial **assessment** was conducted in mid-2025, involving the then fully deployed Regional Office (MENA); in early 2026, an intermediate assessment was conducted involving all three Regions. Progress agis monitored on quarterly basis.

## 3.Objective of the evaluation

The purpose of the evaluation is to provide an independent, evidence‑based assessment of the decentralized organizational model and to generate clear conclusions and strategic recommendations to inform future organizational directions. As such, its main purpose is to inform the **learning process**; it does however pursue objectives of external and internal accountability (strategic, managerial, and financial). The evaluation will:

- Assess how well the decentralized organizational model supports the organization’s mission, strategy, and objectives
- Identify strengths, limitations, and risks inherent in the model
- Provide practical recommendations for improvement or adaptation

The specific objectives are to review and analyze:

- The relevance and strategic alignment of the decentralized organizational model, in particular the achievements against the six objectives of the decentralization project.
- Cross-region **system coherence** and **adaptation** to context, including the potential for cross-fertilization\*\*.\*\*
- The effectiveness and efficiency of **governance**, management, and operational arrangements, including the existing **process** framework (steering mechanisms, including decision‑making, accountability, and coordination), **resource use** and cost‑effectiveness.
- **Organizational culture**, ways of working, change management, and attitude to change.
- **Risks**, mitigation measures and future considerations.

## 4.Scope of the evaluation

Given the breadth of themes and organizational dimensions covered by this evaluation, the assessment is expected to focus on **strategic and systemic analysis** rather than an exhaustive review of all processes, functions and organizational units. The evaluation should examine the extent to which the decentralized organizational model is fit for purpose, identify key achievements, challenges, enabling factors and risks, and generate evidence-based insights to **inform future decision-making**. The Consultant is expected to balance depth and breadth appropriately, prioritizing areas of greatest relevance to organizational effectiveness, governance, sustainability and achievement of the decentralization objectives.

The evaluation will cover:

- Key processes
- Management and operational roles and responsibilities
- Relevant interdependencies
- Periodic implementation reviews
- Decision‑making and accountability arrangements
- Resourcing (financial, human, …) and efficiency
- Organizational culture, leadership, and power dynamics

Out of scope (unless otherwise specified):

- Individual programme/project impact or sectoral effectiveness.
- Detailed financial audits or compliance reviews.

## 5.Intended users of the evaluation, stakeholders & informants

The **intended users** of the evaluation findings include all Terre des hommes staff at country, regional and HQ levels and the Foundation Board, in addition to key external stakeholders, such as selected strategic and/or local partners and institutional donors.

**Key stakeholders** and informants include:

- **Country level**: country directors, selected coordinators, first-responder and junior staff, local partners
- **Regional level**: regional directors, regional coordinators and support staff
- **HQ level**: sector staff (experts, all departments)

Key informants include **former Tdh staff** who were involved in the design and/or roll-out of the decentralized organizational model.

The evaluation results will inform the Tdh decentralized organizational model standard operating procedures; these will replace the 2023 Decentralization Guidance accordingly.

## 6. Evaluation Criteria and questions

Criterion:

- Criteria : Relevance -> Question: To what extent has the Project adequately targeted the real needs of the organization, allowing for existing constraints, potential and strengths?
- Criteria : Coherence -> Question: How well does the Project fit with other similar approaches in the aid sector? What good practice can be integrated? To what extent is the cross-region system coherent, and how can it be improved?
- Criteria : Effectiveness -> Question: To what extent have the Project’s objectives been met?
- Criteria : Efficiency-> Question: Have available resources been utilized in the best way?
- Criteria : Impact-> Question: What difference does the Project make? What are its broader, long-term effects (both intended and unintended, positive or negative)?
- Criteria : Sustainability-> Question: Will the system last (foresight analysis)?

## 7. Methodology

The consultant is free to define their methodology in dialogue with the team that accompanies the evaluation; the proposed methodology will be presented in an **inception report**, which will be examined and approved by the Tdh Evaluation Steering Committee.

The proposed methodology will address the following items:

- Analytical framework (evaluation matrix)
    - Stakeholder mapping & engagement plan
    - Data collection (methods and tools)
    - Organizational model mapping
    - Analysis & synthesis
    - Judgment:

i) **options** (scenarios/future models) and

ii) resulting actionable **recommendations**

- Working plan, including a timeline

The evaluation will involve visits to Tdh Headquarters, the three Tdh Regional Offices (in Amman/Jordan, Dakar/Senegal and the Europe-Asia Region).

## 8.Deliverables

The consultant is expected to deliver clear, usable evaluation products, as follows.

- Inception (initial) report including a description of the proposed methodology, evaluation matrix, timeline and working plan, initial documentary analysis, and the proposed use of AI for analytical purposes (if any).
- Full report (methods, findings, **options** max 40 pages): v. 1.0
- Executive summary (max. 5 pages)
- Visuals (org maps, decision flows, dashboards)
- Workshop to convert options into **recommendations**.
- Final report (v. 2.0), including follow-up items and summary tables indicating the main conclusions and recommendations, separating:
    - Short-, medium- and long-term items
    - Lessons learned (including items for global standardization, those requiring regional adaptation, and those that should remain locally-defined) and roadmaps
    - **Annexes:** technical details of the evaluation (including clean and raw data, rendered anonymous), terms of reference, surveys protocols and questionnaires, protocols of interviews and observation, tables or graphics, photographs, secondary review references, persons and institutions contacted, a PowerPoint presentation of the findings and recommendations.

## 9.Timeline

- Phase I: desk review and inception report (May 2027)
- Phase II: Field work, presentation and debriefing to the Evaluation Steering Committee (July 2027)
- Phase III: analysis & report (August 2027).
- Phase IV: workshop (conversion of options into recommendations, September 2027)
- Phase V: final report and recommendations (December 2027).

## 10.Roles and responsibilities

The Decentralized Model Evaluation Steering Committee (SC) manages the evaluation at Tdh. It comprises the General Direction and Operations, and reports to the Direction Committee CODIR:

- Sponsor: Director General
- Lead: Chief of Staff
- Members:
    - HQ Operations & Child Rights (1)
    - People & Culture (1)
    - Regional Directors (3)
    - Quality & Accountability Sector (1)

The Steering Committee responsibilities include:

- Approval of the terms of reference for the evaluation;
- Selection of the successful consultant(s): the Steering Committee kindly requests the support of the P&C Department for this item (short listing);
- Pre-departure briefings and information throughout the evaluation;
- Examination and approval of the inception report and subsequent deliverables;
- Management of communications, organization and provision of the documentation required, logistic arrangements as necessary (responsibility and/or facilitation of transport, accommodation, organization of field work), translations;
- Access to material at Tdh Headquarters as necessary (working space, etc.).

The consultant will receive an onboarding briefing and commits to abiding by:

- Specific procedures (e.g. Code of Conduct, behaviour towards the media and security measures).
- Respect for the Child Protection Policy.
- The climate, travel and socio-cultural facts that could influence the collection of data.
- Ethics – confidentiality.

## 11.Profile of the Service Provider (team) qualifications and experience

The assignment requires an independent consultant with strong expertise in organizational development and efficiency, and research within humanitarian, development, and private sectors.

### Qualifications

Advanced university degree (Master's or PhD candidate) in fields such as Business and/or Organizational Development, Public Policy Development, Management Consulting, Public Administration / Nonprofit Management or equivalent.

### Experience and Expertise

The consultant should demonstrate:

- Strong academic and applied research experience
- Proven experience conducting technical assessments, mixed-method evaluations, or validation of governance systems and organizational reform, especially in decentralized and/or locally devolved models
- Experience working in a variety of cultural and business/organizational contexts
- Experience working within humanitarian, development, safeguarding, or child protection-related environments is desirable

### Skills

The consultant should possess:

- Strong analytical and technical research skills
- Excellent writing skills
- Experience in comparative analysis and evidence-based reporting
- Strong facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills
- Ability to synthesize technical findings into actionable recommendations
- Strong cultural sensitivity

### Language

Excellent written and spoken English, and excellent spoken French are required.

title: Event Management Services for Financing Decent Work in Fragile Economies Event
body:
**Event Management Services for Financing Decent Work in Fragile Economies Event**

**In Baghdad, Iraq 30 November 20261**

## Background and rationale:

The International Labour Organization project named “The Promotion of the Development of SMEs” (IRQ/23/05/DEU), funded by KfW on behalf of the German Federal Government, has established Iraq’s first dedicated SME credit-guarantee architecture — the Empowerment Guarantee Fund (EGF), operated by the Iraqi Company for Bank Guarantees (ICBG) under the regulatory oversight of the Central Bank of Iraq. Working through participating financial institutions, the initiative was designed to shift the banking sector’s risk calculus toward small and medium enterprises and to expand access to formal finance under fragile-market conditions. The initiative also works in complementarity with other German (BMZ)-supported efforts in Iraq: the International Organization for Migration (IOM) refers eligible enterprises — including among returnee and displacement-affected communities — to the guarantee facility, connecting vulnerable entrepreneurs to the formal finance the fund unlocks.

Following an initial pilot phase, the project is now moving to full operational launch across all governorates of Iraq. This transition — from pilot to national scale — is a significant institutional milestone. It is also an opportunity to position the initiative where it belongs: not as a stand-alone SME-finance project, but as a practical, working demonstration of the Global Coalition for Social Justice, contributing directly to its thematic area on expanding decent work and sustainable enterprises.

title: Associate Director, Global CRM (Salesforce)
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees made to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries and 28 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. The IRC leads the way from harm to home.

This position sits within Marketing Technology, the team that builds and runs the systems IRC uses to raise funds, engage supporters and advocate for the people we serve. These include the enterprise Salesforce CRM, our donation platforms, the global Rescue.org website and our email communications platforms. Together they underpin the fundraising, communications and advocacy work of External Relations around the world.

**Job Overview / Summary (What and Why):**

IRC’s Salesforce platform sits at the heart of how we raise funds and stay in touch with supporters. It manages a multi-million dollar fundraising operation, is used by around 500 staff, and runs as a single global, GDPR-compliant org built on a heavily customised Nonprofit Success Pack (NPSP). We are now evaluating a potential move to Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud, and exploring how AI, including Agentforce and integrations with models such as Anthropic’s Claude, can work responsibly inside the platform.

The Associate Director will lead that next chapter. Reporting to the Senior Director, Marketing Technology, the postholder owns the platform’s strategy, roadmap and architecture, and plays a central role in how Salesforce evolves at the IRC in the future.

The role brings together three things that rarely sit in one job: architect-level Salesforce judgement, leadership of a technical team, and a real understanding of how a global nonprofit raises and manages income. The postholder leads and develops the CRM team, holds contractors and delivery partners to clear standards of quality, security and supportability, and explains technical choices and trade-offs in plain language to senior leaders.

This is a team leadership role that stays close to the technology. We expect the postholder to spend most of their time on strategy, architecture and leading the team, while remaining hands-on where it matters: designing solutions, reviewing the team’s work and building when the situation calls for it.

**In their first year, the postholder will:**

- Get to know the current NPSP org in depth, including its customisations, integrations and technical debt, and the teams who depend on it.
- Agree a clear platform roadmap and the governance to deliver it with stakeholders across External Relations, Finance and programme teams.
- Identify where AI tools such as Agentforce can add real value, safely and in line with IRC’s data protection and AI governance requirements.
- Shape the team structure, ways of working and partner model the platform needs for its next phase.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Platform strategy and product ownership**

- Act as global product and platform owner for IRC’s Salesforce ecosystem, setting its direction and making the case for investment.
- Develop and maintain a prioritised CRM roadmap aligned with IRC’s fundraising, supporter engagement, finance and programme objectives, and run a fair, transparent process for managing demand.
- Lead IRC’s evaluation of Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud, including the business case, options appraisal and, if approved, the migration strategy and plan.
- Lead the responsible evaluation and adoption of AI within the CRM ecosystem, including Agentforce and integrations with external AI models, identifying worthwhile use cases while meeting IRC’s data protection, security, ethical AI and governance requirements.
- Assess AppExchange and other third-party products and recommend what IRC should adopt, keep or retire.

**Architecture and technical leadership**

- Own the solution architecture of the platform: data model, automation, security model, integrations and managed packages, including NPSP, Account Engagement (Pardot), Outlook integration, Blackthorn and Apsona.
- Set design and build standards for declarative and programmatic development (Flow, Apex, Lightning Web Components, APIs), and review the work of the team and partners against them.
- Reduce technical debt in a heavily customised org, and make sure new work is simpler to support and ready for future platform changes.
- Oversee integrations with donation platforms, finance systems, the data warehouse and reporting tools, so that data flows are reliable and well documented.
- Stay hands-on: prototype, configure and build when that is the fastest way to unblock the team or prove an approach.

**Team and partner leadership**

- Lead, coach and develop a team of Salesforce administrators, developers and a business analyst, including recruitment, performance management, career development and workload planning.
- Build a team culture of good engineering practice, clear documentation and service to the people who use the platform.
- Manage contractors, implementation partners and suppliers, holding them to account for quality, cost and delivery, and contribute to procurement, licensing and budgeting.

**Governance, security and operations**

- Own platform governance: access management, security, audit controls, data quality, business continuity, and compliance with GDPR and other data protection requirements across countries.
- Oversee incident, problem, change and release management, including readiness for Salesforce’s three annual releases and managed-package updates.
- Oversee user support, testing and defect resolution delivered by the team and partners.
- Make sure reports and dashboards give leaders accurate, trusted information.

**Stakeholders and business context**

- Build strong relationships with fundraising, finance, data and programme leaders, and understand how IRC raises, processes and stewards income in different countries.
- Explain technical options, risks and trade-offs in plain language so that senior, non-technical stakeholders can make good decisions.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Senior Director, Marketing Technology

**Position directly supervises:** Team of Salesforce Admins/Developers/Business Analyst

**Other Internal and/or external contacts**:

**Internal***:* Close collaboration with global and regional stakeholders across External Relations, Resettlement, Asylum and Integration, Information Technology, Communications, Finance, Data and Analytics and other teams that rely on the CRM platform.

**External**: Technology suppliers, implementation partners, consultants, contractors and other service providers.

**Job Qualifications:**

**Education:**

**Minimum:**

Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, business systems or a related discipline or equivalent professional experience.

**Preferred:** Salesforce Architect-track certifications (e.g. Application Architect, System Architect), Nonprofit Cloud Consultant, Advanced Administrator, Platform App Builder or Platform Developer I/II.

**Work Experience:**

**Minimum:**

- Significant experience leading an enterprise Salesforce platform in a complex, multi-country organisation, with the architectural judgement to design and govern a large, heavily customised org.
- Experience acting as a product or platform owner, including developing roadmaps, governing demand and prioritising investment.
- Deep knowledge of Salesforce architecture, including data models, automation, security, integration and application lifecycle management, with enough hands-on fluency in declarative and programmatic development to guide and review the work of developers.
- Proven experience managing and developing a team of technical professionals, and overseeing contractors, consultants or delivery partners.
- An understanding of how nonprofits or comparable organisations raise and manage income (such as individual and recurring giving, gift processing and donor data) and how a CRM supports that work.
- Experience overseeing platform operations, including incident, change and release management.
- Experience working with APIs, ETL processes, integration platforms and cross-system data flows.
- Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to explain technical options and risks to non-technical and senior audiences.
- Experience of Agile delivery, using tools such as Git-based source control and Jira.
- Strong analytical thinking, judgement, problem solving ability and customer service orientation.

**Preferred:**

- Hands-on experience with Nonprofit Success Pack and Nonprofit Cloud, ideally including an NPSP-to-Nonprofit Cloud evaluation or migration.
- Experience delivering technology for fundraising, marketing, advocacy or supporter engagement teams.
- Familiarity with Salesforce Account Engagement (Pardot), Data Cloud, Agentforce or comparable marketing, data and AI platforms.
- Experience working with enterprise architecture, DevOps, Business Intelligence, Data Warehousing or integration technologies.
- Experience working with an international nonprofit, humanitarian or mission-led organisation.
- Experience running a CRM across multiple countries and currencies, including under GDPR and other data protection regimes.
- Experience contributing to supplier management, procurement, licensing, budgeting and technology business cases.
- Hands-on development experience with Apex, SOQL and Lightning Web Components.

  
**Working Environment*****:***

A collegiate environment working collaboratively across External Relations and broader IRC. Strong sense of transparency and accountability to ensure we are doing right by our clients and donors, exemplifying the IRC Way.

- This is a fully remote role, with travel 3–5 times per year for in-person time with the team and for learning and development.

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United States of America, United Kingdom, and Kenya.***

**Compensation:** (US Pay Rate: $113,102-$120,000/yr; UK Pay Rate: £69,440-£84,058/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Head of support services (F/M) - Lebanon
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## **MdM in Lebanon**

MdM has been working in Lebanon for 30 years and actively contributed to respond to needs of the most vulnerable communities as the context unfolded (2011 Syrian crisis, 2019 severe economic crisis, 2020 Beirut Blast) and the current period since October 7th, 2023 – especially as the war resumed in Lebanon since March 2nd, 2026.

MdM’s intervention in Lebanon aims to strengthen the national health system and increase access to quality healthcare.

MdM is recognized in Lebanon as a major actor in the areas of mental health (MHPSS) and sexual and reproductive health (SRH). MdM supports several health centers and mobile clinics in the South, Beirut Mount Lebanon, Bekaa, and Baalbek Hermel; and works with other partners.

Despite the June 2026 ceasefire, the situation remains highly volatile and high needs remain, particularly in the South of the country. MdM continues to closely monitor the situation to ensure an appropriate, timely and flexible intervention, always in line with the needs of the various conflict-affected populations.

## **About the role**

You are responsible for the overall strategy and compliance, through the management of logistics, human resources and finance departments in the MdM Lebanon mission.

You ensure support services are fully compliant with MdM policies, donor requirements, national authorities' regulations, and applicable legislation.

## **Who you’ll work with**

Under the line management of the General coordinator, and the technical management of the Desk manager, you work in close collaboration with the other departments: Program, Medical/MHPSS, Grants, Security-Safety-Access, MEAL.

## **What you’ll do**

**Support services leadership & strategic planning**

- Provide strategic leadership and guidance to the General Coordinator and Country Management Team on all support-related matters
- Contribute to country strategy development, annual planning and financial planning processes
- Lead support services planning and ensure alignment between operational and programme priorities
- Anticipate operational challenges and oversee contingency planning to ensure humanitarian response continuity

**Development & reporting**

- Ensure support functions contribute effectively to proposal development, reporting and donor-related processes
- Coordinate the timely provision of analyses and support inputs required for programme development and decision-making

**Support services management & quality**

- Oversee the quality, compliance and performance of all support functions in accordance with organizational policies, donor requirements and local regulations
- Ensure sound resource management, accountability and legal compliance across the mission
- Monitor support systems, identify risks and corrective actions, and strengthen tools and procedures to support informed decision-making
- Promote effective integration and collaboration between Finance, HR, Logistics and programme teams

**Risk management, compliance & internal control**

- Strengthen internal control systems and ensure appropriate management of mission resources
- Identify and mitigate financial, operational, compliance, safeguarding, fraud and corruption risks
- Lead or coordinate audits, investigations and follow up on recommendations in collaboration with relevant stakeholders
- Promote adherence to anti-fraud, anti-corruption and safeguarding policies across the mission

**Team management & capacity building**

- Recruit, manage and develop the support services team through coaching, performance management and capacity-building initiatives
- Foster effective coordination, communication and information sharing across teams
- Identify learning and development needs and ensure access to appropriate technical support and resources

**Coordination & representation**

- Ensure strong coordination between support, programme, field and headquarters teams
- Facilitate effective information sharing and contribute to organizational reporting
- Represent the organization with authorities, partners and donors, alongside the General Coordinator, when required.

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you...**

- Have significant experience in humanitarian operations, including in complex contexts, and have held a senior support coordination role within an international NGO
- Have strong expertise across HR, Finance, Logistics and Administration, ideally supporting health programmes and donor-funded projects
- Are a strategic and analytical leader, able to drive operational performance, manage risks and support decision-making
- Have a proven ability to lead, coach and develop teams while fostering collaboration across departments
- Are organized, adaptable and solution-oriented, with the confidence to make decisions and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment

**This role may not suit you if you...**
