title: Senior Policy Officer – Remote (within the range of ET–CET Time Zones)
body:
PATHWAYS INTERNATIONAL

**Senior Policy Officer**

**About us – what do we do?**

At a time of unprecedented forced displacement and system disruption, we are reforming the global system of safe and legal routes to protection. Our world-class team works closely with leaders and innovators from across sectors in over 20 countries. Together we design, launch, and expand safe and legal routes for displaced people. Together we pilot bold new ideas aimed at making the entire global system of safe and legal routes stronger and more sustainable.

**How we do it**

- We build and lead powerful partnerships and networks.
- We provide trusted advice.
- We accelerate operational delivery.
- We generate and share insights.
- We inspire change.

**About the role – what will you do?**

We are seeking a **Senior** **Policy Officer** to join the powerful global team at Pathways International (PI).

This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to PI’s global strategy on pathways to protection and community sponsorship by working closely with the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and the Executive Chair (EC) as part of the executive office.

The role will include supporting the CEO and the EC in their daily work, which includes high-profile public and private engagements across a wide range of stakeholders, including those at a high political level and within the private sector. We are looking for a strategic thought partner who can proactively project manage multiple high-level strategic mandates in the executive office consistently and on schedule, while supporting the CEO and EC’s time management and achievement of deliverables.

The role will also entail supporting the CEO and the EC in preparing, executing, and following up on key meetings of the organization’s senior executives and the Board.

**Responsibilities**

- **Coordination of strategic initiatives:** Oversee end-to-end coordination of strategic projects, acting as a central point of contact for the CEO and EC to manage and track high-priority  
    timelines, dependencies, and deliverables across the executive office to ensure strategic goals and organizational objectives are met on schedule.
- **Stakeholder management, development and communication support:** Support and coordinate the CEO’s and the EC’s engagements with key PI partners, including with government, the private sector, and other NGOs, in particular to further the organization’s fundraising and development strategy. The candidate must be able to manage high-level stakeholders in a highly professional manner while exercising discretion and good judgment. This role will also entail coordinating PI’s communication on social media channels.
- **Writing and analysis:** Prepare policy and other briefing documents to support the CEO and the EC. Offer executive-level communication support, including drafting and editing of confidential background documents, correspondence and emails.
- **Meeting and event organization**: Collaborate with colleagues to prepare meeting strategy. Prepare agendas; schedule and organize meetings with senior stakeholders, and record and distribute minutes. Communicate with meeting and event participants in a professional and timely manner.
- **Organizational development:** Support the CEO in fostering the organizational development of Pathways International, in particular by integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into PI’s work, with a strong comfort level using AI tools to draft high-quality correspondence and streamline project management processes.

**About you – who are we looking for?**

We are looking for a restless, nimble, and confident team member who can tactfully, strategically and effectively project manage work within the executive office, while contributing to policy analysis and writing at a senior level within a dynamic and fast-paced environment.

- You have a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field—such as public policy, public affairs, political science, or international development; or equivalent professional experience in diplomatic, private sector, political or chief of staff roles.
- You have a proven understanding of one or more relevant fields which may include: forced displacement, refugee protection, global migration, geopolitics and diplomacy.
- You have at least eight years of relevant work experience in a fast-paced work environment, with a preference for direct work with executive offices or similar functions.
- You have strong organizational skills and thrive on project managing executive office projects, meetings and event deliverables and deadlines to enable leadership success critical to the organization.
- You demonstrate strong policy capability, able to research, analyze and draft high-quality briefings and materials for senior stakeholders with keen attention to detail.
- You have excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. Proficiency in other languages, in particular Spanish and Italian, is an asset. Editorial or copyediting experience is also an asset.
- You have excellent interpersonal skills and experience collaborating with people from different backgrounds, countries, cultures and languages.
- You are able to work on a varied and constantly evolving portfolio, while consistently displaying professionalism, discretion, tact and responsibility. You have a strong understanding of confidentiality and need-to-know principles, ideally having directly handled similar sensitive functions.
- You have a strong comfort level using AI tools to draft high-quality correspondence and to inform and strengthen project management processes.
- You are comfortable preparing well-presented PowerPoint and Word documents and using Excel, Zoom, MS Teams and SharePoint.

We encourage applications from qualified candidates with lived experience of forced displacement, migration, or with close personal and cultural connections to refugee communities.

**Location**

This is a full-time **remote position within the range of Eastern Time (ET) to Central European Time (CET)**. The candidate must be available for flexible working hours, including meetings in CET and ET.

Applicants contacted for evaluation will be asked to provide proof that they have the legal right to work in their country of residence. Maintaining such legal right to work in their country of residence is a condition of employment.

**Salary**

Competitive, commensurate with experience.

**Contract**

- One-year term contract (renewable)

**How to apply**

Please submit in English:

- Cover letter
- CV
- Unedited writing sample of no more than five pages.

Please apply through BambooHR at [https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/60](https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/60) by **November 15th, 2026, at 11:59 pm EST** to be considered for this position.

**Equal opportunity employer**

Pathways International is an equal opportunity employer, committed to diversity and inclusion. We encourage applications from qualified candidates of all genders and from all national, religious, and ethnic backgrounds, including persons with disabilities and those with lived experience of forced displacement. We will provide accommodation upon request during the recruitment, selection, and assessment process.

title: International Migration Data Governance Specialist
body:
## **Job Description**

**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

**Project Context and Scope**

The consultancy contributes to the the ‘Awda Amina Phase II: Strengthening Miration Governance in Iraq’ project funded by the European Union and to the ‘Strengthening Data Systems to Improve the Managament of Internally Displaced Persons Referral Systems in Iraq’ project funded by the United Nations Internal Displacement Solutions Fund.   
Under the overall guidance of the Head of Sub-Office (Erbil) and the direct supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research), The consultant will provide specialized technical support and policy-development support to IOM staff working on migration and displacement data governance initiatives under the project portfolio. The consultant will draft technical and policy documents under the supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research) and support technical consultations, workshops, framework development, implementation tracking, and reporting activities, identify technical and policy challenges, and provide recommendations for consideration by the Programme Officer (DTM and Research). All managerial, representational, and decision-making functions shall remain the responsibility of IOM staff.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

  
The consultant will work under the direct supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research) and the overall supervision of the Head of Sub-Office (Erbil).

## **Responsibilities**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

**Data ownership and access**

  
i. Support the development a structured framework that outlines roles, responsibilities and processes for managing migration and displacement data across government ministries and agencies, in both Federal Iraq and KRI.  
ii. Provide technical support and draft clear guidelines for data ownership, access, sharing and utilisation, complying with national policies and promoting adherence with international best practices in terms of data protection.  
iii. Under the supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research) and in consultation with relevant IOM staff, the consultant will provide technical input and draft documentation for consideration by IOM in relation to:  
 i) Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) between relevant ministries and the Central Statistical Office; and  
 ii) data-sharing protocols between Federal and KRG authorities aimed at enhancing collaboration and access to migration-related data.  
iv. Draft a Data Integration Framework and provide technical recommendations regarding its implementation under the supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research), to establish links with the National Referral Mechanism and enable seamless data flow by connecting the digital infrastructure for migration management.

**Data standards**

  
v. Draft a national framework for migration and displacement-related statistical definitions and concepts aligned with international/UN recommendations and standards, integrating inputs from consultations led by IOM staff with relevant national and international partners.  
vi. Develop technical data guidelines and standardized indicators to ensure consistency and comparability across different governmental agencies in the operationalization of agreed definitions.

**Data analysis and use**

  
vii. Utilize secondary data analysis to inform and enhance policy development and facilitate Iraq's participation in international migration data forums.  
viii. Develop recommendations for improved data analysis and reporting on migration and displacement by relevant Ministries, supporting evidence-based policy formulation.  
ix. Prepare briefing materials and provide technical support to IOM staff for intra- and inter-ministerial workshops led by IOM staff.Draft recommendations, publication schedules, and other technical documents to facilitate the publishing of periodic statistics on government-owned websites to ensure public availability of migration data.

**Other**  
x. Perform any other duties as may be assigned.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

• Agreed outputs set out in the ToRs are delivered in a timely manner and to a satisfactory quality standard.  
• Technical outputs produced by the consultant result in measurable improvements in data governance practices.

## **Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

• Master’s degree in law, economics, political science, public policy, demography/statistics, or a related field with at least five years of relevant professional experience, or Bachelor’s degree with seven years of professional experience.  
• Proven experience in migration data governance through previous work with government bodies, international organizations or think tanks.  
• Familiarity with international statistical standards such as the International Recommendations on IDP Statistics and the Recommendations on Statistics of International Migration and Temporary.  
• Familiarity with IOM’s Data Protection Principles and with othe international data protection frameworks and best practices.  
• Familiarity with the Iraqi context and government institutions.  
• Strong writing and communication skills; experience in facilitating multi-stakeholder workshops and in drafting policy framework, guidelines and technical standards.  
• Fluency in Arabic and English.

**Languages**

For this consultancy, excellent command of English is required.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Travel required**

Yes

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Mission France - Responsable de la promotion et de la médiation en santé F/H
body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Responsable de la promotion et de la médiation en santé pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et l’Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre opérations de secours et plaidoyer.

**Votre rôle :**

Sous la responsabilité du·de la Référent·e du projet pluridisciplinaire Migration, et en lien fonctionnel avec les responsables de la protection, des activités médicales et de la santé mentale de l’unité migration, vous piloterez la stratégie de promotion et de médiation en santé et d’engagement communautaire.

Vous encadrerez les médiateur·rices en santé et les médiateur·rices interculturel·les, superviserez les interventions de terrain et contribuerez à adapter les activités du projet aux besoins et aux retours des personnes accompagnées.

Votre fonction associera pilotage stratégique, management d’équipe, mobilisation communautaire et présence opérationnelle sur le terrain.

**Principales responsabilités :**

**Définir et mettre en œuvre la stratégie de promotion et de médiation en santé**

- Concevoir, déployer et actualiser la stratégie de promotion de la santé, de médiation et d’engagement communautaire, en lien avec le·la Référent·e du projet pluridisciplinaire Migration.
- Définir les priorités, les activités, les outils et les modalités de suivi en fonction des besoins identifiés et de l’évolution du contexte.
- Garantir une approche participative, en associant les personnes accompagnées et les communautés à l’identification de leurs besoins et à l’élaboration des réponses.
- Superviser la création de supports de prévention et d’éducation à la santé, adaptés aux différents publics, en veillant à leur pertinence, à leur validation et à leur accessibilité linguistique et culturelle.
- Contribuer aux réflexions stratégiques et opérationnelles du projet, en collaboration avec les responsables des autres pôles.

**Piloter les activités communautaires et les interventions de terrain**

- Organiser et superviser les activités d’« aller-vers », les actions de sensibilisation, les ateliers collectifs et les activités de médiation individuelle.
- Veiller à la qualité des interventions menées sur les lieux de vie, lors des activités collectives et dans le lieu de répit.
- Développer des approches favorisant l’écoute, la confiance et la participation des personnes aux décisions qui concernent leur santé.
- Superviser la surveillance à base communautaire, notamment l’identification des besoins et des situations préoccupantes, la recherche active de cas et l’orientation vers les services de santé adaptés.
- Accompagner les médiateur·rices dans l’organisation des entretiens individuels et des rencontres communautaires.
- Coordonner, avec les autres responsables de pôles, les évaluations rapides des besoins et les interventions nécessitant une approche pluridisciplinaire.

**Manager, accompagner et développer les compétences de l’équipe**

- Encadrer les médiateur·rices en santé et les médiateur·rices interculturel·les, et organiser leurs plannings en fonction des activités du projet.
- Participer aux recrutements, à l’intégration et à l’évaluation des membres de l’équipe, en collaboration avec le département des ressources humaines.
- Identifier les besoins de formation et mettre en œuvre un plan de développement des compétences associant formation, accompagnement individuel, coaching et partage de pratiques.
- Superviser la qualité des activités, notamment les méthodes participatives, les techniques pédagogiques, l’écoute active et l’utilisation des outils de médiation.
- Favoriser la coopération, la circulation des informations et la complémentarité entre les équipes, tout en assurant la continuité des activités en cas d’absence.

**Analyser les besoins et renforcer les liens avec les communautés et les partenaires**

- Mettre en place des dispositifs de recueil et d’analyse des retours des personnes et des communautés, notamment des perceptions, préoccupations et rumeurs liées à la santé.
- Contribuer aux évaluations rapides, aux enquêtes et à l’analyse qualitative des besoins individuels et des dynamiques communautaires.
- Développer et actualiser une cartographie participative des communautés, des associations et des acteurs du territoire, en intégrant les observations des équipes de maraude.
- Entretenir les relations avec les partenaires et partager les informations utiles à l’adaptation des interventions.
- Superviser la collecte des données, analyser les tendances, produire les rapports d’activité et documenter les enseignements tirés des interventions.
- Utiliser ces analyses pour proposer des ajustements opérationnels et améliorer la pertinence des actions de promotion et de médiation en santé.

**Garantir la sécurité, la qualité et les moyens nécessaires aux activités**

- Assurer la fonction de point focal sécurité pour les équipes lors des interventions  
    d’« aller-vers ».
- Veiller à l’application des mesures de safeguarding dans l’ensemble des activités et à leur bonne compréhension par les membres de l’équipe.
- Garantir le respect des principes, protocoles et standards de Médecins Sans Frontières.
- Planifier et suivre les ressources humaines, matérielles et financières nécessaires au fonctionnement du pôle, en collaboration avec les départements concernés.
- Contribuer à l’amélioration continue des pratiques et à la capitalisation des expériences du projet.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Licence en sciences sociales, sciences du comportement, santé publique, médiation en santé ou santé communautaire, ou diplôme d’infirmier·ère en santé communautaire.
- Une expérience significative dans l’accompagnement de publics vulnérables et le management d’équipe peut également correspondre au profil recherché.
- Au moins deux ans d’expérience professionnelle dans la gestion de programmes ou de projets de médiation en santé ou de santé communautaire, en France, à l’étranger ou au sein de MSF.
- Expérience indispensable dans l’utilisation de méthodes qualitatives.
- Expérience requise dans la conception, la mise en œuvre et le suivi de stratégies.
- Expérience en management d’équipe.

**Compétences et qualités :**

- Solides capacités d’analyse, de réflexion stratégique et d’adaptation des interventions aux réalités du terrain.
- Aptitude à encadrer, accompagner et faire progresser une équipe.
- Sens de l’écoute, qualités relationnelles et capacité à instaurer un dialogue avec des publics divers.
- Capacité à travailler en équipe pluridisciplinaire et à coopérer avec différents partenaires.
- Sens de l’organisation, orientation vers les résultats et exigence de qualité.
- Engagement envers les principes de promotion de la santé et de Médecins Sans Frontières.
- Flexibilité et capacité à évoluer dans des environnements difficiles et changeants, y compris lors d’activités de nuit.
- Permis B souhaité.

**Langues et outils :**

- Maîtrise du français indispensable.
- Bonne maîtrise de l’anglais souhaitée.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques courants : Word, Excel et Internet.
- La connaissance de logiciels de traitement de données qualitatives (NVivo), de création graphique (Photoshop), de collecte de données ou de cartographie (KoboCollect, OsmAnd, QGIS) constitue un atout.

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Mobilité exigée sur le Littoral Nord entre Calais et Dunkerque**

 Statut non-cadre : **CDD de 12 mois renouvelable**

**Rémunération et avantages :**

- **3 425,87 € brut mensuel sur 13 mois** 22 jours de RTT par an.
- Titres-restaurant de 12 € (prise en charge MSF à 60 %)·
- Prise en charge à 50 % des transports en commun ou des kilomètres à vélo

**Poste à pourvoir : 4 janvier 2026**

title: Mission France - Coordinateur.rice de projet adjoint.e F/H
body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Coordinateur.rice de projet adjoint.e pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et en Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre opérations de secours et plaidoyer.

**Votre rôle :**

Aux côtés du ou de la coordinateur·rice de projet, vous participerez au pilotage des opérations, à l’organisation des activités et à l’accompagnement des équipes dans un contexte exigeant et en constante évolution. Vous contribuerez à l’analyse des besoins et des risques, à la coordination des interventions et à la qualité de la prise en charge. En l’absence du ou de la coordinateur·rice de projet, vous assurerez la continuité de la coordination.

Vous assisterez également le ou la coordinateur·rice de projet dans la planification, la coordination et le suivi des activités de MSF sur le Littoral Nord, afin de garantir une réponse cohérente, sûre et adaptée aux besoins des personnes exilées.

**Principales responsabilités :**

Favoriser une communication claire et respectueuse entre les personnes accompagnées et les équipes MSF, en atténuant les barrières linguistiques, les incompréhensions culturelles et les discriminations, afin de contribuer à un accès équitable à des soins et à un accompagnement adaptés.

**Vos principales responsabilités :**

**Contribuer à la coordination des opérations sur le terrain**

- Participer à la transition des projets de Calais et Dunkerque vers un projet Littoral Nord intégré.
- Contribuer à l’organisation et au suivi des activités sur les lieux de consultation, les lieux de survie et les plages ou zones de départ.
- En l’absence du ou de la coordinateur·rice de projet, assurer la coordination des activités et la continuité opérationnelle.
- Organiser, avec les responsables de pôle, la participation des équipes aux maraudes de prévention et de prise en charge des personnes lors des tentatives de traversée.
- Veiller à l’application des protocoles opérationnels et de sécurité, notamment les briefings et débriefings et les procédures liées aux distributions.
- En lien avec le ou la référent·e pluridisciplinaire du projet Migration, contribuer à la coordination entre les équipes et à la qualité de la prise en charge, dans le respect du secret médical partagé et des standards MSF.

**Analyser le contexte et contribuer à la représentation de MSF**

- Participer au suivi du contexte politique, humanitaire et sécuritaire à la frontière et faire remonter les évolutions susceptibles d’affecter les opérations.
- Contribuer aux missions exploratoires sur le littoral, notamment en dehors des zones d’intervention actuelles de Calais et Dunkerque, afin d’identifier les besoins et les priorités.
- Assurer le lien avec les acteurs du littoral et participer aux réunions de coordination.
- En collaboration avec le ou la coordinateur·rice de projet, contribuer à la représentation de MSF auprès des autorités, des services publics, des forces de l’ordre, des associations, de la société civile et des médias.
- Participer aux actions de communication et de plaidoyer liées aux interventions de MSF sur le littoral.

**Accompagner les équipes et veiller à la sécurité**

- Contribuer à l’organisation des ressources humaines, à l’intégration du nouveau personnel, au suivi quotidien des équipes et à l’identification des besoins de formation.
- Participer à l’analyse des risques et à la mise à jour des consignes de sécurité ; être le point focal sécurité lors des interventions selon les responsabilités définies pour le projet.
- Soutenir les équipes dans la mise en œuvre des activités et assurer la transmission des informations opérationnelles.
- Promouvoir les principes de safeguarding et veiller à leur compréhension et à leur application au sein de l’équipe et du projet.

**Assurer le suivi, la qualité et le reporting des activités**

- Superviser ou contribuer à la compilation et à l’analyse des données collectées, ainsi qu’au reporting des activités.
- Veiller au respect des standards MSF et à la qualité de la prise en charge pendant les interventions, notamment en matière de distributions et de safeguarding.
- En collaboration avec le ou la coordinateur·rice de projet, contribuer à l’accompagnement des équipes de support, notamment logistique et RH/finance.
- Participer à l’identification de pistes de plaidoyer en lien avec la présence de MSF lors des tentatives de traversée.

**Profil recherché**

- Diplôme universitaire de niveau bac+3 minimum.

title: Consultant – Comparative, Gender-Sensitive and Youth-Inclusive Assessment of Georgia’s Diaspora Engagement Policy & Institutional Framework
body:
**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration  
**Duty Station of the Consultancy**: Tbilisi, Georgia. Remote assignment - 2 missions to Georgia envisaged for the presentation of preliminary findings and participation in the validation of the final report.

**Duration of Consultancy:** 24 November 2026 – 8 April 2027 (20 working days).

**Nature of the consultancy:** Conduct an international comparative, gender-sensitive and youth-inclusive assessment of diaspora engagement policies, institutional arrangements and practices, and to contribute to evidence-based recommendations for strengthening Georgia’s diaspora engagement framework.

The international consultant (IC) will specifically contribute international comparative expertise, identify relevant global good practices and provide methodological and analytical input to the Georgia-specific review undertaken jointly with the national consultant.

**Project Context and Scope**

Georgia has a large and diverse diaspora community worldwide whose knowledge, skills, networks, investments and other resources represent an important potential contribution to the country’s social and economic development. According to international estimates, nearly half a million Georgian-born migrants live abroad, while the broader diaspora is considerably larger and geographically dispersed across Europe, North America and other regions. Georgia’s diaspora represents a significant source of human, social, cultural and economic capital that can contribute to innovation, investment, entrepreneurship, knowledge transfer and local development.

Over the years, the Government of Georgia has implemented a range of initiatives aimed at maintaining ties with Georgian communities abroad and promoting diaspora engagement, including diaspora outreach programmes, grant schemes, cultural initiatives and institutional coordination. However, existing efforts remain fragmented, and there is a need for a more comprehensive, evidence-based, gender-sensitive and youth-inclusive approach that can respond to the evolving profile, needs and aspirations of diaspora communities.

To address these challenges, IOM is implementing the project “Georgia’s Global Diaspora Engagement Initiative for National Development”, which aims to strengthen the enabling environment for effective and sustainable diaspora engagement and support greater contributions of diaspora communities to national development. The project seeks to institutionalize diaspora engagement as a core component of Georgia’s development agenda through strengthened policies, institutional arrangements, coordination mechanisms, and innovative approaches to diaspora investment, innovation and knowledge exchange.

As part of this effort, IOM will undertake a comprehensive policy and institutional analysis of diaspora engagement in Georgia. The analysis will assess existing policy frameworks, institutional arrangements, coordination mechanisms, and stakeholder engagement practices, while also examining opportunities for strengthening diaspora participation in national development processes. Particular attention will be paid to the meaningful engagement of women and young diaspora members and to identifying international good practices relevant to the Georgian context. The policy and institutional analysis will serve as a foundational activity under the project and will provide the evidence base for strengthening policy coordination, identifying institutional gaps and opportunities, supporting stakeholder consultations, and informing future strategic planning on diaspora engagement. The assignment will contribute to ensuring that diaspora engagement policies and mechanisms are evidence-based, inclusive, and aligned with international good practices while remaining responsive to the specific needs and priorities of Georgia.

Under the direct supervision of the IOM Programme Manager, the IC will provide an comparative, gender-sensitive and youth-inclusive assessment of diaspora engagement policies, institutional arrangements and practices, identify relevant global good practices and provide methodological and analytical input to the Georgia-specific review, to contribute to evidence-based recommendations for strengthening Georgia’s diaspora engagement framework.

The consultant will undertake the following tasks:

A. Develop the methodology and analytical approach and review relevant materials

- Review the existing analytical and policy framework for diaspora engagement in Georgia, as well as relevant project documentation and materials provided by IOM, with the support of the national consultant.
- Develop an inception report with the findings from the literature review and methodology for assessing diaspora policies and institutional arrangements from an international comparative perspective.
- Ensure that gender equality and meaningful youth participation are integrated throughout the methodology.
- Agree with IOM and the national consultant on the workplan, division of responsibilities and approach to consultations.

B. Conduct an international comparative review

IC will review selected international and global approaches to diaspora engagement, with particular attention to: a) diaspora policy and strategy development; b) institutional and coordination mechanisms; c) diaspora consultation and representation; d) engagement of diaspora professionals, entrepreneurs and investors; e) mobilization of diaspora knowledge, skills and networks; f) youth diaspora engagement and women’s participation.

IC will identify relevant global good practices and innovative approaches. Analyse the conditions under which these practices have been effective and assess their relevance and applicability to the Georgian context.

C. Contribute to the policy and institutional analysis of Georgia

With the support of and in close coordination with the National Consultant, the International Consultant (IC) will provide international comparative, methodological and analytical expertise to the assessment of Georgia’s diaspora engagement policy and institutional framework. The IC will ensure that the Georgia-specific assessment is informed by relevant international experience and good practices, while remaining responsive to Georgia’s institutional, policy and socio-economic context.

The IC will:

- Contribute to the assessment of Georgia’s existing diaspora engagement policy and strategic framework, including relevant legislation, policies, strategies, action plans and other key government and institutional documents, with a focus on their objectives, scope, implementation arrangements, coherence and alignment with broader national development priorities.
- Assess the institutional architecture for diaspora engagement, including the mandates, roles and responsibilities of relevant government institutions and other key stakeholders involved in diaspora affairs. Particular attention will be given to institutional coordination, division of responsibilities, information-sharing and mechanisms for ensuring a coherent and whole-of-government approach to diaspora engagement.
- Examine existing mechanisms and practices for diaspora consultation, participation and representation, including opportunities for diaspora communities and diaspora organizations to contribute to policy development, programme design, implementation and monitoring. The assessment should consider the extent to which existing mechanisms enable meaningful, inclusive and sustained engagement.
- Provide comparative perspectives on Georgia’s institutional and coordination arrangements, drawing on the international comparative review undertaken under this assignment. The IC will identify relevant models and approaches from other countries and assess their potential relevance and applicability to the Georgian context, taking into account differences in institutional structures, diaspora profiles and national circumstances.
- Assess existing approaches to mobilizing diaspora human, social, professional, financial and knowledge resources, including mechanisms for engaging diaspora professionals, entrepreneurs, investors, researchers and other skilled members of the diaspora in national and local development. Where relevant, the assessment should consider existing or potential mechanisms for knowledge transfer, investment, innovation, entrepreneurship and skills exchange.
- Identify key policy and institutional gaps, overlaps, coordination challenges and opportunities affecting effective diaspora engagement in Georgia. This should include consideration of the enabling environment, institutional capacity, stakeholder coordination, outreach and communication mechanisms, and the sustainability and effectiveness of existing engagement approaches.
- Assess the inclusiveness of the existing diaspora engagement framework, with particular attention to the participation and representation of women and young diaspora members. The assessment should identify structural, institutional or practical barriers to their meaningful participation and highlight opportunities and entry points for strengthening their engagement in policy processes, programmes, investment, entrepreneurship, knowledge exchange and other forms of national development.
- Contribute to the identification of priority areas for strengthening Georgia’s diaspora engagement framework, drawing on evidence from the Georgia-specific assessment, stakeholder consultations and international comparative experience. Recommendations should be practical, context-sensitive and, where possible, linked to specific institutional or policy entry points.
- Work closely with the National Consultant to ensure complementarity between the international comparative and Georgia-specific components of the analysis, jointly review emerging findings, and integrate relevant national evidence and stakeholder perspectives into the comparative assessment.

Gender equality, youth inclusion and meaningful participation of diverse diaspora groups should be systematically integrated across all aspects of the analysis rather than treated as stand-alone considerations.

D. Support consultations and validation processes

The consultant will support IOM and the national consultant in preparing and conducting:

- Stakeholder consultations, validation workshops and IWG meetings, including contributing consultation methodologies, agendas and guiding questions.
- Prepare presentations and analytical materials;
- Facilitate and/or co-facilitate discussions and incorporating stakeholder feedback into the final report.

Based on the policy and institutional review, international comparative analysis and stakeholder consultations, the consultant will contribute to a set of practical recommendations, based on evidence and international experience, aimed at strengthening Georgia’s diaspora engagement framework

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**  
Georgia’s Global Diaspora Engagement Initiative for National Development

**Category B Consultants: Tangible and measurable outputs of the work assignment**

- **Deliverable 1**: Inception Report, with Methodology and Analytical Framework. A concise inception report to be submitted by 8 December 2026.
- **Deliverable 2**: International Comparative Review of Diaspora Engagement Policies and Practices with institutional and coordination models and special focus on diaspora youth and women engagement, mobilization of diaspora knowledge, skills and resources, to be submitted by 29 January 2027.
- **Deliverable 3**. Analytical Inputs to the Joint (with the National Consultant) Policy and Institutional Review, including comparative assessment of Georgia’s existing framework, key policy and institutional gaps, opportunities and entry points, gender and youth considerations and comparative lessons relevant to Georgia to be submitted by 15 March 2027.
- **Deliverable 4**: Final report with actionable recommendations, validated by the stakeholders, to be submitted by 8 April 2027.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- Delivers the listed deliverables on time and with good quality.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Advanced postgraduate degree (i.e., PhD, MA, MSc) in Demography, Economics, Sociology, Statistics, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Public Affairs, and/or other disciplines relevant to the assignments.
- **Experience & Skills**
- Demonstrated experience in research, policy analysis, comparative policy analysis, developing policy recommendations and/or programmatic work related to the migration, development area.
- Demonstrated experience in diaspora engagement, migration and development, migration governance or related fields.
- Knowledge of diaspora engagement policies and institutional models in different regional contexts would be an advantage.
- Experience conducting assessments on migration and development, preferably in Eastern Europe, or South Caucasus.
- Proficiency in qualitative and quantitative research methodologies, including field data collection, stakeholder consultations, and policy analysis.
- Previous engagement with government institutions, international organizations, or NGOs on migration and development issues.
- Demonstrated ability to work in English, with excellent oral and written communication skills.

**Travel required**

- Remote assignement, with two missions to Georgia envisaged for the presentation of preliminary findings and participation in the validation of the final report. Consultancy fee will cover all travel and other expenses of the consultant and shall constitute the only financial entitlement which will be disbursed to the consultant.

**Languages**

- For this consultancy, excellent command of English is required.
- Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

- IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.
- **Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:
- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.
- **Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators
- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

title: Consultant for conducting the assessment and development of three bilateral public health SOP packages for priority Points of Entry in Lao PDR
body:
**FOR THE CONSULTANCY CONTRACT OF: \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

1. **Duty Station of the Consultancy:** Vientiane, Lao PDR, with approved travel to selected provinces and Points of Entry
2. **Duration of Consultancy:** 6 months from contract start; exact dates to be agreed at contract signature
3. **Nature of the consultancy:** Assessment and development of three bilateral public health SOP packages for priority Points of Entry in Lao PDR / Category B Consultancy (selected)
4. **Project Context and Scope:**

The 24-month project “Enhancing National Pandemic Preparedness and Cross-Border Health Security in Lao PDR” (PRIMA Code LA10P0566; Project Code MP0745), starting 01 October 2026, supports national and provincial authorities to strengthen pandemic preparedness and cross-border health security. Outcome 2 focuses on strengthening legislation and policy frameworks for priority pathogens. Output 2.1 commits to expanding endorsement and operationalization of bilateral coordination SOPs and cross-border data-sharing protocols with Viet Nam, Thailand, and China.

Scope of responsibilities

Under the project’s health component, the consultant will:

- Review existing public health surveillance, event notification, verification, risk assessment, response coordination, referral, and information-sharing arrangements for the Lao PDR–Thailand, Lao PDR–Viet Nam, and Lao PDR–China corridors.
- Recommend 1 Lao-side priority Point of Entry (PoE) for each corridor, with a rationale. IOM Lao PDR and the relevant authorities will confirm the sites and scope during inception.
- Identify operational gaps and clarify the roles, triggers, communication channels, timelines, safeguards, escalation, and follow-up needed for practical bilateral coordination.
- Develop 3 bilateral SOP packages, tailored to the confirmed corridor and PoE, and consult relevant authorities on the drafts.
- Align the review with applicable national procedures and bilateral arrangements; relevant IHR (2005) provisions—including Articles 19, 21 and 22 and Annex 1, Part B, as applicable—and WHO guidance on PoE core capacities and public health emergency contingency planning.
- Support technical validation, document feedback and unresolved decisions, and provide handover guidance for the Lao project team.

The NO-A will coordinate government and technical engagement; the G5 Project Assistant will support administrative arrangements; and IOM Thailand MHU will provide budgeted technical support. Competent authorities retain decision-making and formal endorsement authority. The assignment is limited to SOP-related procedures; it is not a nationwide or full IHR capacity assessment and does not determine PoE designation. After handover, the IOM Lao PDR project team will coordinate follow-up toward endorsement and operationalization. DRCMU flow-monitoring work is outside this consultancy.

**5. Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing:** **Migration Health Unit**

IOM Lao PDR, in coordination with the Ministry of Health and relevant border, immigration, and counterpart-country authorities; Pandemic Fund project LA10P0566, “Enhancing National Pandemic Preparedness and Cross-Border Health Security in Lao PDR.” IOM Thailand MHU provides technical support to IOM Lao PDR.

**6. Category B Consultants: Tangible and measurable outputs of the work assignment (with realistic delivery dates)**

1. **Deliverable 1** – Inception report | Due within 1 months of contract start | Payment: 30% upon written acceptance. The report will set out the methodology, document review, consultation plan, assessment framework, and workplan for all 3 corridors. It will recommend 1 Lao-side priority PoE for each corridor with rationale; identify preliminary priority events/pathogens and stakeholders; provide the common SOP outline, drafting approach, validation and travel schedule; and state assumptions, risks, mitigation measures, and decisions required. IOM Lao PDR and relevant authorities will confirm the 3 sites and scope before detailed assessment begins. The inception report will explain how relevant IHR provisions and WHO PoE guidance will inform the assessment and drafting.
2. **Deliverable 2** *–* Consolidated assessment and draft SOP packages | Due by Month 4 | Payment: 60% upon written acceptance. Submit a consolidated assessment of the 3 confirmed corridors and PoEs, including current process maps, roles and responsibilities, operational gaps, and recommendations, together with 3 draft bilateral SOP packages using a common structure and country- and PoE-specific procedures. Each draft will cover event triggers, notification channels and timelines, verification and risk assessment, coordination and response, information-sharing safeguards, referral and follow-up where applicable, escalation and after-hours contacts, records, closure, and review. Include consultation records, draft forms or job aids, a comment log, and validation-session materials; provide editable files and clean PDFs. Include a concise IHR/WHO alignment and gap matrix for each package, mapping relevant IHR provisions and WHO guidance to the draft procedures, current arrangements, identified gaps, and recommendations.
3. **Deliverable 3** – Final validated SOP package and handover | Due by Month 6 | Payment: 10% upon written acceptance. Submit the final assessment and recommendations and 3 complete SOP packages incorporating consolidated technical comments and documented validation for each package. Include relevant forms, concise job aids, an updated contact-list template, a response-to-comments matrix, unresolved decisions and endorsement steps, and a handover/implementation plan identifying sequence, proposed institutional responsibilities, resource and coordination needs, monitoring indicators, contact updates, and periodic review. Brief the Lao project team and designated government counterparts and provide editable source files. Formal government endorsement is not guaranteed by the consultant and is not a condition of payment where it depends on government decisions outside the consultant’s control; endorsement steps and decisions must be documented. Include the updated IHR/WHO alignment and gap matrix for each package, noting remaining gaps and any policy or institutional decisions for the competent authorities.

**7. Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

**Deliverable 1: Inception report**

- Submitted within the agreed timeframe and includes the required methodology, document review, consultation plan, assessment framework, and workplan.
- Provides a clear rationale for the proposed Lao-side PoE in each of the 3 corridors, identifies preliminary stakeholders and priority public health events, and sets out how the sites and scope will be confirmed with IOM Lao PDR and the relevant authorities.
- Presents a practical common SOP structure and explains how relevant IHR provisions and WHO PoE guidance will inform the assessment and drafting.
- Identifies key assumptions, risks, mitigation measures, validation arrangements, and decisions required to proceed.

**Deliverable 2: Consolidated assessment and draft SOP packages**

- Provides an evidence-based assessment of the 3 confirmed corridors and PoEs, including process maps, roles and responsibilities, operational gaps, and recommendations.
- Includes 3 draft bilateral SOP packages, using a common structure and procedures tailored to each corridor and PoE.
- Each draft clearly describes relevant event triggers, responsible actors, notification channels and timelines, verification and risk assessment, coordination and response, information-sharing safeguards, referral and follow-up where applicable, escalation, and record-keeping and review arrangements.
- Includes a concise IHR/WHO alignment and gap matrix for each package, limited to the SOP-related procedures, and supporting consultation records, draft forms or job aids, a comment log, and materials for validation.
- Submits complete and editable files in the agreed formats by the agreed deadline.

**Deliverable 3: Final validated SOP package and handover**

- Provides 3 complete SOP packages revised in response to consolidated technical comments, with validation outcomes and any unresolved decisions documented for each package.
- Includes the updated IHR/WHO alignment and gap matrices, relevant forms and job aids, and an updated contact-list template.
- Provides a practical handover and implementation plan that identifies proposed responsibilities, sequence of follow-on actions, resource and coordination needs, monitoring indicators, contact-update arrangements, and periodic review.
- Briefs the IOM Lao PDR project team and designated government counterparts and submits complete, editable final files by the agreed deadline.
- Clearly identifies formal endorsement steps that remain for the competent authorities; government endorsement itself is not a consultant performance requirement where it depends on decisions outside the consultant’s control.

**8. Education, Experience and/or skills required**

- Advanced university degree in public health, epidemiology, health systems, health security, international health, or a related field.
- At least 7 years of relevant professional experience in public health preparedness, surveillance, border health, health emergency coordination, or development of operational procedures.
- Demonstrated experience assessing or developing SOPs, notification protocols, data-sharing procedures, referral pathways, or emergency coordination mechanisms.
- Experience facilitating multi-agency consultations and translating technical requirements into practical procedures for frontline and management levels.
- Knowledge of IHR (2005), public health surveillance and response systems, and cross-border health coordination. Experience in Lao PDR or the Mekong region is an advantage.
- Strong analytical writing, facilitation, and project coordination skills. Fluency in English is required; Lao language ability is an advantage. Interpretation and translation arrangements will be coordinated with IOM.

**9. Travel required**

Travel within Lao PDR to the 3 confirmed PoEs and, as needed, to other agreed locations for consultations and validation activities is expected. All travel is subject to IOM approval, security clearance, and the agreed workplan.

**10. Competencies**

**Values**

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage:** demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy:** shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies – behavioural indicators**

- **Teamwork**: develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

title: Call for Experts – ICT, GIS, Digital Transformation, AI and Information Management
body:
## Background

Innovation Consulting & Solutions (ICS) is a women-led international consultancy specialising in digital transformation, information management, software development, artificial intelligence, data analytics and technical assistance for humanitarian, development and institutional clients.

ICS has experience developing and implementing enterprise management systems, digital beneficiary management platforms, e-voucher solutions, community feedback mechanisms, data collection tools, dashboards and AI-enabled applications.

To support its growing portfolio of ICT projects and upcoming consultancy opportunities, ICS is expanding its network of national and international technical experts.

We are inviting qualified professionals with demonstrated experience in developing, implementing and supporting institutional information systems to join our expert roster.

## Areas of Expertise

Applicants should have proven experience in one or more of the following areas.

### 1. GIS, GeoWeb and Spatial Information Systems

- Senior GIS and WebGIS Specialists
- GIS/Web Application Developers
- Spatial Database Developers and Administrators (PostgreSQL/PostGIS)
- Geospatial Data Engineers and GIS Analysts
- QGIS, OpenLayers, Leaflet and GeoServer Specialists
- GIS Operations and Spatial Data Management Specialists
- Urban Planning and Housing Information System Specialists
- Remote Sensing and Earth Observation Specialists
- Geospatial Dashboard and Interactive Mapping Developers
- GIS Data Quality, Metadata and Validation Specialists

Experience developing open-source GeoWeb platforms, integrating spatial datasets, managing geographic layers and implementing web-based spatial monitoring systems is particularly relevant.

### 2. Enterprise Systems, CRM and Digital Transformation

- Digital Transformation and ICT Strategy Consultants
- Enterprise and Solution Architects
- Senior Business Analysts and Requirements Engineering Specialists
- Customer Relationship Management (CRM) Specialists
- Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Specialists
- Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Business Central Specialists
- Microsoft Power Platform Consultants
- Microsoft 365, Outlook and SharePoint Integration Specialists
- Organisational Workflow and Business Process Automation Specialists

### 3. Artificial Intelligence and Data Science

- AI Chatbot Developers
- Data Scientists and Predictive Analytics Specialists

### 4. Cybersecurity, Cloud and IT Infrastructure

- Cybersecurity and Information Security Specialists

- Identity and Access Management Experts
- Microsoft Entra ID and SSO Specialists
- GDPR and Data Protection Consultants

## Scope of Potential Assignments

Depending on the requirements of individual assignments, selected experts may contribute to:

- ICT assessments, feasibility studies, system architecture and technical design.
- Development and implementation of CRM, ERP and institutional information management systems.
- Development of GIS-enabled web applications, spatial databases and geographic information platforms.
- Integration of GIS layers, survey platforms, databases and reporting dashboards.
- Development of interactive maps, urban planning information systems and spatial monitoring tools.
- Database design, migration, data validation and integration.
- Development of AI-enabled applications and decision-support tools.
- Cybersecurity assessments, data protection compliance and secure cloud or on-premises deployment.
- Software development, quality assurance, testing and user acceptance.
- Technical training, capacity strengthening and knowledge transfer.
- System maintenance, troubleshooting, documentation and operational support.

## Required Qualifications and Experience

Candidates should demonstrate:

- A university degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, GIS, Geoinformatics, Data Science, Cybersecurity or another relevant discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
- At least five years of relevant experience for specialist roles. Senior expert and team leadership positions may require seven to ten years or more.
- Demonstrated experience delivering relevant technical assignments, preferably for institutional or international clients.
- Strong technical expertise and practical knowledge of the relevant technologies, tools and frameworks.
- Ability to produce high-quality technical documentation and deliver agreed outputs within project timelines.
- Experience working with UN agencies, international NGOs, development institutions, government entities or public-sector organisations is an advantage.
- Experience in Syria and the wider MENA region is particularly valuable for country-specific assignments.
- Professional proficiency in English. Arabic is highly desirable for Syria-based assignments.

title: Mission France - Responsables des activités de santé mentale F/H
body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Responsable des activités de santé mentale pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte:**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et en Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre action médicale, coordination opérationnelle et plaidoyer.

**Votre rôle :**

Sous la responsabilité du·de la Référent·e du projet pluridisciplinaire Migration, et en lien fonctionnel avec la Référente santé mentale de l’Unité Migration, vous assurerez la coordination, la supervision et le suivi des activités de santé mentale du projet.

Vous encadrerez les psychologues, garantirez la qualité des prises en charge et contribuerez à l’adaptation des interventions aux besoins identifiés sur le terrain.

Votre fonction associera **pilotage opérationnel, supervision clinique, management d’équipe et contribution aux orientations stratégiques du projet**.

**Vos principales responsabilités :**

## **Définir et piloter les activités de santé mentale**

- Identifier et analyser les besoins en santé mentale des personnes accompagnées et contribuer à l’élaboration de la stratégie du projet.
- Planifier, organiser et adapter les activités de soutien psychologique et psychosocial, individuelles et collectives, en fonction des besoins et de l’évolution du contexte.
- Garantir l’application des protocoles et standards MSF, ainsi que la qualité des interventions réalisées dans les structures de soins et sur les lieux d’intervention.
- Participer, avec la Référente santé mentale de l’Unité Migration et le·la Référent·e du projet, à l’élaboration et à l’actualisation des protocoles, outils et supports techniques, conformément aux recommandations sanitaires applicables.
- Superviser la prise en charge des situations complexes et veiller à ce que les personnes nécessitant un soutien psychiatrique bénéficient d’une orientation et d’un suivi adaptés, y compris pour les traitements prescrits.
- Contribuer aux discussions stratégiques et opérationnelles afin d’adapter les interventions aux réalités du terrain.

**Manager, accompagner et développer les compétences des équipes**

- Encadrer les psychologues et organiser leurs plannings entre consultations, activités collectives et interventions d’« aller-vers ».
- Assurer, en collaboration avec les ressources humaines, le recrutement, l’intégration et l’évaluation des membres de l’équipe.
- Identifier les besoins de formation et mettre en œuvre un plan de développement des compétences associant supervision, coaching et partage de pratiques.
- Apporter un appui technique et organiser des formations en santé mentale pour les équipes pluridisciplinaires et les partenaires du projet.
- Veiller à ce que les médiateur·rices et les interprètes intervenant lors des consultations disposent des connaissances et des repères nécessaires pour assurer une communication adaptée.
- Favoriser la coopération, la communication interne et le respect d’une posture professionnelle neutre, indépendamment des convictions personnelles.

**Renforcer les parcours de soins et la coordination pluridisciplinaire**

- Favoriser une prise en charge globale des personnes en collaboration avec les équipes médicales, de travail social et de médiation.
- Participer aux réunions pluridisciplinaires de gestion de cas et accompagner la recherche de solutions pour les situations complexes ou prioritaires.
- Développer et actualiser une cartographie des services de santé mentale, des structures spécialisées, des associations et des partenaires du territoire.
- Renforcer les mécanismes d’orientation internes et externes, en tenant compte de l’accessibilité et des capacités de prise en charge des services existants.
- Entretenir des relations régulières avec les partenaires institutionnels, associatifs et sanitaires afin de faciliter la continuité des accompagnements.
- Identifier et documenter les obstacles à l’accès aux soins, notamment les insuffisances des dispositifs de prise en charge d’urgence après des événements traumatiques.

**Analyser les résultats et garantir la qualité des interventions**

- Superviser la collecte et l’analyse des données relatives aux activités de santé mentale, en veillant à leur fiabilité.
- Définir et suivre les indicateurs, évaluer les résultats et produire les rapports d’activité nécessaires au pilotage du projet.
- Analyser les problématiques rencontrées par les psychologues et les résultats des évaluations rapides des besoins afin d’améliorer les pratiques et les orientations.
- Identifier les problématiques susceptibles d’alimenter les actions de plaidoyer de MSF et les transmettre au·à la Référent·e du projet.
- Contribuer à la planification et au suivi des ressources humaines, matérielles et financières nécessaires aux activités, en lien avec les départements support.
- Veiller à l’utilisation adaptée des ressources et à l’amélioration continue de la qualité des prises en charge.

**Profil recherché :**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Master ou diplôme en psychologie, ou diplôme de médecine avec spécialisation en psychiatrie et inscription obligatoire à l’Ordre des médecins.
- Au moins deux ans d’expérience professionnelle en tant que psychologue ou dans une fonction similaire.
- Expérience dans un projet portant sur la migration.
- Expérience en management d’équipe.

**Compétences et qualités :**

- Solides compétences en santé mentale, en coordination d’activités et en accompagnement des équipes.
- Capacité à superviser les pratiques professionnelles et à développer les compétences des collaborateur·rices.
- Sens de l’écoute, rigueur et exigence de qualité.
- Capacités d’analyse et aptitude à adapter les interventions aux besoins identifiés.
- Esprit d’équipe et capacité à travailler en pluridisciplinarité.
- Gestion du stress, flexibilité et capacité d’adaptation à des environnements difficiles et changeants.
- Adhésion aux principes et aux valeurs de Médecins Sans Frontières.
- Permis B souhaité.

**Langues et outils :**

- Maîtrise du français indispensable.
- Bonne connaissance de l’anglais souhaitée.
- La maîtrise d’autres langues est fortement appréciée.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques courants : Word, Excel et Internet.

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Mobilité exigée sur le Littoral Nord entre Calais et Dunkerque**

 Statut non-cadre : **CDD de 12 mois renouvelable**

**Rémunération et avantages :**

- **3 425,87 € brut mensuel sur 13 mois** 22 jours de RTT par an
- Complémentaire santé prise en charge à 100 % par MSF·
- Titres-restaurant de 12 € (prise en charge MSF à 60 %)·
- Prise en charge à 50 % des transports en commun ou des kilomètres à vélo
