title: Coordinateur de site et du consortium Fonds Humanitaire (F/H) - République Centrafricaine
body:
Vous souhaitez intégrer une association militante et agir concrètement pour plus de justice sociale ?

Médecins du Monde agit depuis plus de 40 ans pour soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, dénoncer les entraves à l’accès aux soins et faire évoluer durablement les politiques de santé.

En France et dans près de 30 pays, nos actions s’articulent autour de six combats politiques :

- droits et santé sexuels et reproductifs (dont le droit à l’avortement)
- migration, exil, droits et santé
- réduction des risques
- santé environnement
- droits et système de santé
- espaces humanitaires

## Médecins du Monde en RCA

La République centrafricaine (RCA) demeure confrontée à des conflits armés récurrents, entraînant une crise humanitaire majeure et de nombreuses violations des droits humains et du droit international humanitaire.

Présente dans le pays depuis 2013, Médecins du Monde (MdM) France intervient auprès des populations les plus vulnérables à travers des soins de santé dans les zones reculées, des services de santé sexuelle et reproductive, la prise en charge des survivant·e·s de violences basées sur le genre (VBG) et le déploiement de cliniques mobiles d’urgence. En 2025, ses interventions ont bénéficié à 278 113 personnes.

Récemment, MdM a renforcé sa présence opérationnelle avec le lancement, en novembre 2024, d’un projet à Batangafo dédié à la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë sévère chez les enfants et des survivant·e·s de VBG. En mars 2026, une nouvelle base a été ouverte dans la sous-préfecture de Kabo, grâce au financement de la DG ECHO, afin d’appuyer six formations sanitaires, dont l’hôpital secondaire, pour une durée de seize mois.

Pour les prochaines années, MdM prévoit d’accroître ses activités, ses financements et sa couverture géographique, tout en consolidant son positionnement comme acteur de référence dans le domaine de la santé, notamment en matière de prévention et de prise en charge des VBG. L’organisation poursuit également sa collaboration avec les autres ONG internationales afin de renforcer la coordination humanitaire, le partage d’informations et l’efficacité des interventions.

## Pourquoi nous avons besoin de vous

En tant que coordinateur de site et du consortium Fonds Humanitaire (F/H), vous aurez pour principales missions de piloter et de coordonner la stratégie et la mise en œuvre des programmes du consortium Fonds Humanitaire à Batangafo, Bouca, Kabo et Sido, en animant les équipes et les partenaires, en garantissant l'application des procédures MdM et en développant le plaidoyer et les partenariats.

Vous assurerez l’animation du consortium entre MdM et Solidarités International sur la base.

## Vos missions

Plus spécifiquement, vos responsabilités seront les suivantes:

## 1. Coordination, représentation et partenariats

- Représenter MdM auprès des autorités, acteurs humanitaires, bailleurs, partenaires techniques et forces présentes dans la zone d’intervention
- Participer aux mécanismes de coordination, ateliers, conférences et visites institutionnelles afin de renforcer le positionnement de MdM
- Assurer des relations régulières avec les partenaires et veiller à la cohérence des actions menées sur la zone

## 2. Pilotage stratégique et gestion du consortium

- Diriger le consortium, animer la gouvernance, coordonner les membres et garantir une prise de décision efficace et transparente
- Définir, suivre et actualiser les plans d’action, de contingence et de suivi-évaluation (MEAL), tout en veillant à la bonne utilisation des ressources
- Produire des analyses, recommandations et retours d’expérience permettant d’améliorer la qualité des interventions et la coopération opérationnelle

## 3. Supervision opérationnelle et suivi des projets

- Organiser et coordonner les activités de la base de Batangafo, y compris les projets, la construction des infrastructures et les relations avec les partenaires
- Piloter la planification des activités, suivre les indicateurs, les échéances contractuelles et l’exécution des actions afin d’assurer leur qualité et leur conformité
- Contribuer à la définition des orientations stratégiques, assurer le reporting opérationnel et capitaliser les enseignements tirés des interventions

## 4. Gestion de la sécurité et de l’accès humanitaire

- Assurer une veille contextuelle et sécuritaire, collecter et partager les informations nécessaires à l’analyse des risques
- Élaborer, actualiser et faire appliquer les dispositifs de sécurité, tout en sensibilisant les équipes aux procédures et règles en vigueur
- Garantir l’accès humanitaire, gérer les incidents de sécurité et coordonner les réponses opérationnelles et les communications en cas de crise

## 5. Management des équipes et supervision des fonctions support

- Encadrer les équipes de la base : recrutement, intégration, fixation des objectifs, évaluation des performances, accompagnement et développement des compétences
- Favoriser la cohésion d’équipe, gérer les conflits, faire respecter les politiques internes et prendre les mesures correctives nécessaires
- Superviser les volets RH, financiers, administratifs et logistiques de la base, notamment le budget, le suivi des ressources et le respect des procédures internes

## Vos collègues

Sous la responsabilité hiérarchique du coordinateur général (F/H) basé à Bangui, vous collaborez avec l’équipe de coordination de MdM à Bangui et les chefs de base des ONGs membres du consortium ainsi le chef d’Antenne OCHA de Batangafo et tous les responsables des ONGs Internationales et nationales présente à Batangafo. Vous supervisez directement les responsables des équipes support et programmes.

## Vous êtes la bonne personne si…

- Vous êtes diplômé.e d'une formation supérieure en gestion de projet ou généraliste de l’Humanitaire
- Vous avez obligatoirement une expérience réussie de trois ans minimum sur un poste similaire de coordinateur terrain au sein d'ONGi en appui de programmes humanitaires financés par des bailleurs intstitutionnels
- Vous avez une expérience réussie en ouverture de base (fortement souhaité)
- Vous avez une expérience réussie en élaboration, conduite et évaluation de projet de santé d’urgence dans des pays et/ou zones en crise
- Vous avez une expérience réussie dans la gestion de la sécurité et de l'accès dans un contexte sécuritaire volatile
- Vous avez une expérience significative en management d'équipe
- Vous êtes capable d'arbitrer en cas de dilemme de manière structurée et méthodique
- Vous savez faire preuve de proactivité, d'organisation et de planification
- Vous parlez couramment le français et l'anglais
- Vous avez une bonne maîtrise du Pack Office et des outils de travail collaboratifs

## Ce poste n’est pas pour vous si...

- Vous craignez ne pas vous retrouver dans les valeurs et le positionnement militant de Médecins du Monde
- Vous ne vous sentez pas à l'aise pour vivre et travailler dans des conditions de vie relativement simples, voire spartiates
- Vous n'avez pas d'expérience de travail en équipe interculturelle et multidisciplinaire
- Vous ne savez pas faire preuve de patience, diplomatie et pédagogie

## **Les prochaines étapes**

Si votre candidature est sélectionnée, nous vous contacterons rapidement pour vous proposer un entretien RH avec un.e chargé.e de recrutement. Les entretiens, technique et managérial, auxquels des cas pratiques pourront éventuellement être intégrés, auront lieu dans le courant du mois de novembre.

Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, des vérifications d’antécédents sur listes internationales pourront être effectuées. Les données sont traitées de façon confidentielle et sécurisée. Plus d’infos : [http://bit.ly/3CSThBs](http://bit.ly/3CSThBs)

Un extrait de casier judiciaire (B3) sera demandé à toute personne recrutée.

## Nous attendons votre candidature

Nous n’avons besoin que de votre CV et de votre lettre de motivation.

Si vous pensez correspondre à ce poste, postulez !

## Vos conditions d’emploi

**Contrat & statut :**

- Salaire brut mensuel 3 663 €
- CDD à pourvoir à partir du 1er novembre jusqu'au 30/08/2027 (non glissant)
- Départ seul

Cadre de travail :

- Poste basé à Batangafo
- Déplacements à prévoir sur la zone du projet (Sido, Batangafo Kabo et Bouca) et à Bangui

Les avantages :

- 13e mois (pour les salarié.e.s ayant plus de 6 mois d’ancienneté)
- Prime d’expatriation de 10% du salaire brut par mois
- Prise en charge du transport (domicile – mission), des visas, des vaccins
- Hébergement: vous serez hébergé.e en guest house (bon niveau de confort)
- Politique R&R: tous les trois mois
- Assurance santé (participation à 50% de MdM et 50% du salarié)
- Assurance rapatriement
- MdM favorise la formation et la mobilité interne

Les indispensables :

- 5 semaines de congés + 22,5 RTT par an
- Engagement fort en faveur de l’inclusion et de la lutte contre toutes les discriminations
- Plus d’infos : [https://bit.ly/3x5MezL](https://bit.ly/3x5MezL)

Diversité et inclusion

MdM s’engage pour l’insertion des personnes en situation de handicap et lutte contre toutes les discriminations.

Si vous bénéficiez d’une reconnaissance de la qualité de travailleur.se handicapé.e et/ou si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement de poste, n’hésitez pas à nous en faire part.

title: MHPSS Advisor
body:
Are you an experienced Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) professional with a passion for advancing evidence-based MHPSS practice in humanitarian settings? Danish Red Cross (DRC) is looking for a MHPSS Advisor to provide technical expertise, capacity development, and quality assurance to the Red Cross Red Crescent National Societies (RCRC) National Societies delivering community-based MHPSS interventions in humanitarian settings.

**About the position and the assignments**

You will be based at the Danish Red Cross HQ in Copenhagen and will be part of the Health Team in the Technical Quality and Impact Unit of the International Department. The Health Team comprises technical advisors within health and mental health and psychosocial support. It ensures the availability of the necessary technical capacities to provide timely and relevant assistance and advice to DRC-supported operations, with a primary focus on the Africa, while also supporting MHPSS interventions in MENA, Europe and Asia regions as needed.

As a member of the Health Team, you will be working under the line management of the Health Team Lead and will also work closely with other colleagues at the DRC HQ and Regional and Country Offices (COs), as well as with NSs staff and volunteers. You will also collaborate with the colleagues from the International Federation of the Red Cross Red Crescent (IFRC) and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). The position does not have programme management responsibilities but supports programmes through technical accompaniment, mentoring, and quality assurance.

**Your main responsibilities will be to:**

- Strategic planning and direction: Contribute to defining and rollout of DRC’s strategic directions within MHPSS in humanitarian settings. Support development and rollout of strategies, policies, and technical frameworks for MHPSS in humanitarian settings.
- Technical support and guidance: Provide evidence-based guidance and advice to DRC COs and National Societies on MHPSS priorities, approaches and activities, remotely or through country visits and missions to ensure that MHPSS interventions follow industry standards and good practice. Support development or adaptation and rollout of relevant technical tools and guidelines to meet operational needs.
- Strengthening of capacities: Support National Societies in assessing technical capacity needs, and in designing and implementing capacity-strengthening plans, including trainings, coaching, mentoring, and technical supervision.
- Program monitoring and evaluation: Support planning and undertaking of assessments, baselines, endlines, reviews and evaluations, and monitoring of MHPSS interventions.
- Advocacy: In close collaboration with relevant humanitarian diplomacy (HD) colleagues, contribute to DRC’s policy influencing, advocacy and HD efforts on MHPSS in humanitarian settings.
- Resource mobilisation: Support proposal development by contributing to the design and quality assurance of MHPSS components in the project proposals that align with donor requirements and organisational goals and priorities.
- Partnerships and collaboration: Foster thematic partnerships and joint MHPSS initiatives within the RCRC Movement and with external stakeholders.
- Surge deployments: Undertake MHPSS surge/deployments in support of DRC bi-lateral operations and wider RCRC Movement responses, including multilateral deployments with the ICRC and the IFRC.

**Your profile**

We are looking for an experienced MHPSS professional with at least five years of experience working on community-based MNHPSS with humanitarian and development organisations, including at least three years in international postings in Africa and MENA regions. You hold a master's degree, or equivalent experience, in MHPSS, social sciences, or another relevant field. You have sound technical, strategy and advisory skills within community-based MHPSS in humanitarian settings and migration. You have proven experience developing and adapting technical guidance, tools and training materials, as well as designing and facilitating capacity-development initiatives for staff and volunteers of partner organisations.

You have experience supporting assessments, technical reviews, evaluations, and the development of quality assurance processes for community-based MHPSS interventions. You are an excellent facilitator and communicator with strong interpersonal and cross-cultural skills. You work collaboratively, are well organised, and are able to manage multiple priorities while meeting deadlines. You are willing and able to undertake field missions, including emergency deployments, with travel of up to four months per year. Professional working proficiency in both English and French is required. Experience of working for the International RCRC Movement is considered an asset.

**We offer**

A job with an opportunity to improve the lives of the most vulnerable people around the world. We further offer a unique opportunity to influence the strategic development and mainstreaming of MHPSS in humanitarian settings.

The position is a full-time position - 37 working hours per week. The position is 12 months with possibility for extension.

Salary and employment conditions are in accordance with Danish Red Cross’s collective bargaining agreement with HK and AC, depending on experience and qualifications. The position is based at the Danish Red Cross headquarters in Copenhagen and requires on-site presence. As this is a national position based in Denmark, the salary package does not include relocation assistance to Denmark and housing or family-related allowances.

**Your future workplace**

The International Red Cross and Red Crescent network is the largest humanitarian network in the world, with a presence and activities in almost every country. All Red Cross and Red Crescent activities have one central purpose: to help those who suffer, without discrimination, whether during conflict, in response to natural or man-made disasters, or due to conditions of chronic poverty. Our work is guided by seven fundamental principles: humanity, impartiality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality.

DRC’s international department’s approx. 300 staff supporting RCRC NSs with planning and implementing humanitarian and development interventions in some of the most challenging contexts in 20 countries across Africa, MENA, Asia, and Europe.

We offer a meaningful work at a purpose-driven workplace with truly engaged colleagues. We focus on professional challenges, well-being and a flexible organising of your work life. All of us contribute to a great work environment and colleagueship.

title: Request for proposals : provision of WIBA plus and group personal accident insurance policy & employer’s liability insurance
body:
**Background**

Tdh is present in Kenya since 2011. Currently Tdh is providing protection services for children and families affected by migration, natural crises and poverty in Dadaab, Kakuma refugee camps, in Garissa and Turkana County respectively, and in Kiambu for child’s rights business in Kiambu County

## The Need/Purpose

TDH provides WIBA Plus & GPA insurance & Employer’s Liability coverage for its employees across the country. TDH is now soliciting detailed proposals from eligible insurance firms to provide WIBA Plus & GPA Insurance for its staff. **The staff number will be subject to change due to staff leaving and staff being hired**.

## Salaries and number of Staff

Details for number of staff as at October 2026 of staff is 52 at an accumulative gross salary of 11,029,041.22 broken down into below categories.

- **Category 1.** 48 Office Workers

Gross Salary Kshs 10,756,899.47

- **Category 2**. 4 Drivers

Gross Salary Kshs. 272,141.75

## Scope of Work/ Service Outcomes

TDH requires extensions provided to cover the following cases/incidents; and all proposals should provide limits on but not limited to the items below.

**GROUP LIFE**

- Accidental Death Benefit – 3 Times annual salary
- Permanent Total Disability - 3 Times annual salary
- Critical illness – 30% of sum Assured to a maximum of 10,000,000.00.
- Last Expense
    - Last expense Main Member – Kshs.300,000.00
    - Coffin and Hearse – Kshs.100,000.00
    - Dependent’s last expense - Kshs.100,000.00
    - Free Cover Limit Kshs 25,000,000.00

**WIBA/GPA**

- Accidental Death Benefit – 8 Times annual Gross salary
- Accidental/ Occupational Permanent Total Disability - 8 Times annual Gross salary
- Temporary Total Disability (Accidental) – Salary up to a maximum of 104 weeks
- Medical Expenses Reimbursement Benefit – Maximum Kshs.800,000.00
- 24 hour cover
- Death as a result of accident or natural causes
- Death as a result of pandemic (e.g COVID-19)
- Permanent disability as a result of accident or critical illness
- Temporary disability as result of accident or illness
- Medical expenses
- Mobility artificial appliances
- Repatriation of mortal remains
- Funeral expenses
- Extension to cover riots, strikes, civil commotions, burns and disfigurements
- Disappearance
- Terrorism extension (Death or Injuries)
- Exclusion of post-mortem report requirement.
- Worldwide Cover
- Inclusion of motor cycling as a driver or passenger but not as racing/sporting
- Inclusion of football, rugby, lawn tennis, badminton.

**EMPLOYER’S LIABILITY**

Limit of Liability

- Limit per person: Kshs. 10,000,000.00
- Any one event Kshs. 25,000,000.00
- Any one period Kshs. 50,000,000.00

## Note to Quote:

Please quote rate applicable for:

- Premium for year 2027 and proposal for 2027
    - Policy excess.
    - Short term Cover or pro rata premium calculation.
    - refund of premium when staff leave.
    - refund policy of medical expense incurred when staff use other medical providers.
    - Please quote any free rider or cover

## Timelines for compensation

The insurance provider upon being notified of applicable accident or scheduled disease shall submit all required documentation within two days and payment shall be made no more than One Month from the date of receiving all documentation submitted by TDH.

## Duration of Cover

The successful Company will enter into a contract with TDH for a period of TWO (2) years. This contract will be renewed based on performance and availability of funding.

**Reporting**

We expect a quarterly report to indicate number of accidents reported, those processed and those outstanding and any recommendations. We do expect minimal TDH staff involvement in processing claims and thus should have a dedicated account holder to help.

## Adding and deletion of Members

Staff who join during the policy year should be added on cover on a pro rata basis. Staff who leave the organization during the policy year should be deleted and reimbursement made for the remaining period.

**Criteria for Proposal Evaluation.**

**Technical Proposal**

Each bidder shall submit a technical proposal addressing the services required and clearly demonstrating how they will meet TDH’s needs.

The proposal will be evaluated according to the following criteria:

- Benefit coverage.
- Claim Settlement timeline.
- Technical support Competency
- Demonstrated Capacity to meet required deliverables.
- Quality of service (ng systems)

**Financial Proposal.**

The financial proposal shall be evaluated according to the price structure proposed.

**Other required Competencies/Skills.** The successful bidder should have.

- Extensive experience and a proven track record in the Life insurance business – List of top 3 clients in the last 3 years is required.
- Sound experience in servicing international organizations – Proof of association with an INGO in Kenya
- Ability to provide 24-hours service.
- Real time administrative support systems – Ability to assign an account manager.
- NO INSURANCE BROKERS

title: Iraq Country Director
body:
## IRAQ COUNTRY DIRECTOR

### FULL-TIME - ERBIL, IRAQ

#### ABOUT FREE TO RUN

Free to Run’s mission is to advance gender equity globally through running. We are a registered nonprofit/nongovernmental organization that has been operating community-led programs for adolescent girls and young women since 2014. We are known for delivering long-term, youth-led, progressive running, leadership, rights, and health programs directly to adolescent girls and young women living in protracted conflict zones. However, the longer-term impact of our work is building enduring social change - decreasing barriers to public participation, increasing women in leadership, and making power structures more equitable and inclusive. Free to Run identifies as an organization working at the intersections of feminism, human rights, development, and humanitarian interventions.

In 2027, we will begin to execute on a new three-year strategic plan which has the organization positioned to grow in a multitude of directions - programmatically, operationally, financially and geographically. The achievement of our mission will continue to be rooted in our work across three strategic pillars: direct service (EMPOWER), capacity building for local NGOs (EQUIP), and building a global movement of activists who are passionate about gender equity and running (MOVE).

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

The Iraq Country Director is responsible for overseeing all aspects of the organization’s work in Iraq – from big picture to the small details. The Country Director is responsible for building the Free to Run network in the country, with a specific focus on donor-relations to achieve fundraising goals and grow the organization’s profile. The Country Director reports directly to the (internationally-based) Executive Director.

**CORE ACCOUNTABILITIES**

**1) Develop and Manage an Effective and Informed Iraq Country Strategy (10%)**

- Envision a high-impact Iraq strategy that aligns with Free to Run’s global strategy
- Develop and track key performance indicators related to strategy
- Participate in organizational strategic planning, budgeting and performance reporting activities

**2) Oversee Free to Run Programs (20%)**

- Oversee program development and design efforts for Iraq-based programs, with support of Senior Program Officer who will directly manage program cycles, currently designed to be operating in three provinces by 2023
- Ensure all programs are adequately staffed and resourced, support staff training and development
- Oversee safe and high-quality program implementation, monitor day-to-day activities of Program staff
- Ensure all programs are monitored and evaluated using standard instruments, work closely with the Executive Director to improve current data collection tools to provide more accurate and timely information on project indicators for success
- Lead program learning and analysis activities with staff, contribute to global learning practices
- Develop and maintain relationships with key local, regional and national stakeholders to ensure smooth operations
- Ensure program data and learning is shared with other relevant staff for program improvement, external reporting and communications

**3) Grow and Lead a High-Performing Team (30%)**

- Lead recruitment, interviewing, hiring and on-boarding/off-boarding of Iraq Free to Run team
- Manage Senior Program Officer and Finance and Operations Officer (others as deemed necessary for growth and as resources allow)
- Ensure the organization and employees comply with all relevant in-country employment laws and best practices
- Coordinate the bi-annual goal setting and performance review processes for all administrative employees and support a culture of constant feedback and learning through targeted coaching and mentoring organization-wide
- Support visits from international staff, Board members and volunteers

**4) Oversee Country-level Finances and Operations (20%)**

- Develop and manage organizational country budget and finances as well as program budgets for specific projects
- Work with bookkeeper to manage administration of expenses, handling of cash and procurement processes, and accounts payable and receivable
- Prepare timely, high-quality financial and narrative reports
- Ensure financial compliance with national and local laws, as well as Free to Run’s finance policies
- Ensure all office operations are functional, with support from Finance and Operations Officer
- Liaise with Executive Director on a regular basis to ensure financial cohesion
- Confirm all registrations and permits to operate as an NGO are up to date, secure licenses to operate in new geographies as needed

**5) Build Support for Free to Run in Iraq (20%)**

- Identify, cultivate and follow through on funding opportunities across sectors, including mapping potential funding opportunities, meeting with potential and current partners and developing funding proposals (with support from the Executive Director)
- Use strong storytelling and persuasion skills to build individual and community support for Free to Run in Iraq amongst key stakeholders
- Compile and prepare Iraq case studies and stories, provide regular input to Free to Run’s social media channels
- Communicate regularly with Free to Run’s community partners and coordinating their participation in events
- Represent Free to Run at influential events and speaking engagements locally, regionally and internationally
- Write press releases and editorial content for website and earned media opportunities

LOCATION

The Country Director position is based in Erbil (KRI) with an expectation of travel to other parts of Iraq regularly and international travel on occasion. Must have a passport and/or residency permit that allows for travel throughout (federal) Iraq and KRI.

**WORKING HOURS**

The Country Director position is a full-time role, estimated at 40 hours per week. Due to the nature of the organization’s business, hours may fluctuate outside regular core hours (Sunday–Thursday; 9AM-5PM), with the possibility of some nights or weekends, depending on the needs of the organization.

**COMPENSATION**

Based on experience. Aligned with market rate for a Country Director in Iraq. (Free to Run uses MSF Salary Survey as one of a handful of benchmarks for salary calculations in Iraq).

**EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES**

Below is what we are looking for as we evaluate applications. Candidates *don’t need to have all these experiences* *and competencies* but should be able to display strengths across multiple areas.

Free to Run seeks an experienced, values-driven leader with a demonstrated ability to mobilize resources, build strategic partnerships, and lead high-performing teams. The successful candidate will combine strong knowledge of Iraq's civil society and development landscape with a commitment to feminist leadership, human rights, and locally-led development. We recognize that strong leaders bring diverse professional and educational experiences.

**Education and Language:**

- Bachelor's degree in international development, human rights, women’s/gender studies, public health or MHPSS, nonprofit management, business administration, or a related field required. An advanced degree is preferred; equivalent relevant professional experience may be considered.
- Professional fluency in written and spoken English is required.
- Professional fluency in Kurdish (Sorani or Kurmanji/Badini) or Arabic required; proficiency in both is strongly preferred.

**Professional Experience:**

- Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in international development, humanitarian assistance, human rights, civil society, or related sectors, including at least three years in a senior management or leadership role.
- Demonstrated track record of successful fundraising and resource mobilization in Iraq and/or the wider Middle East region, including personally cultivating donor relationships, securing institutional or private funding, and developing successful funding proposals or partnerships.
- Established relationships with, and strong understanding of, the regional donor landscape, including bilateral and multilateral donors, foundations, international NGOs, and private-sector funding partners.
- Proven experience leading, managing, and developing diverse teams, including responsibility for staff performance, professional development, organizational culture, and effective team collaboration.
- Experience managing organizational budgets, operational systems, and financial accountability, including compliance with donor requirements and applicable national regulations.
- Deep understanding of Iraq's political, social, cultural, and operating environment, including the Kurdistan Region, and demonstrated ability to navigate complex stakeholder relationships.
- Experience engaging with government authorities, civil society organizations, institutional donors, and community-based partners.
- Experience working in women's rights, gender equity, youth leadership, refugee and displacement, or community-based development programming strongly preferred.
- Experience managing institutional grants and working within international NGO accountability, safeguarding, and compliance frameworks preferred.
- Experience working in collaboration with a global headquarters and other country-teams strongly preferred

**Skills, Leadership Approach and Competencies:**

Feminist and Rights-Based Leadership

- Demonstrated commitment to feminist principles, gender equality, and human rights, with the ability to translate these values into everyday leadership, management practices, and organizational decision-making.
- Proven ability to lead through an empowering, inclusive, and participatory management approach that shares power appropriately, encourages staff agency and ownership, values diverse perspectives, and creates opportunities for individual and collective leadership.
- Ability to foster a respectful, psychologically safe, and accountable working environment in which team members feel empowered to raise concerns, challenge ideas constructively, and contribute meaningfully to decisions.
- Strong understanding of power dynamics, discrimination, and structural inequalities, with the ability to apply intersectional and culturally responsive approaches to staff management, partnerships, and programming.
- Commitment to safeguarding, prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (PSEAH), non-discrimination, and the dignity and rights of staff, participants, and communities.

Fundraising and External Relations

- Excellent relationship-building, networking, and negotiation skills, with the confidence and credibility to engage senior government officials, institutional donors, private-sector partners, and civil society leaders.
- Strong fundraising and business development capabilities, including donor cultivation, strategic positioning, proposal development, and negotiation of funding partnerships.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including persuasive writing, public speaking, and the ability to represent Free to Run effectively with diverse audiences.
- Ability to identify and pursue strategic opportunities that strengthen Free to Run's financial sustainability, institutional credibility, and influence.

Strategic and Operational Leadership

- Strong strategic thinking and planning skills, with the ability to translate organizational priorities into achievable country-level objectives, operational plans, and measurable results.
- Demonstrated ability to balance strategic leadership with sound financial management, operational oversight, and organizational accountability.
- Strong judgment, integrity, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to make sound decisions in complex, politically sensitive, and rapidly changing environments.
- Ability to lead organizational change constructively, foster innovation, and build a culture of continuous learning and improvement.
- Strong cross-cultural communication, emotional intelligence, and conflict-resolution skills, including the ability to provide constructive feedback, address performance challenges fairly, and navigate difficult conversations with professionalism.
- Ability to collaborate effectively within a globally distributed organization, maintaining clear communication, mutual accountability, and alignment between country-level and global teams.
- Proficiency with standard digital collaboration, communication, and financial management tools, including Google Workspace and Microsoft Office.

**PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES**

The successful candidate will demonstrate integrity, humility, resilience, sound judgment, and a genuine commitment to Free to Run's mission. They will be a confident external representative and an empowering internal leader who understands that effective leadership is measured not only by organizational results, but also by the capacity, confidence, and agency developed in others.

*Free to Run is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We don’t just accept differences — we celebrate, support and thrive on them for the benefit of our team, our programs, and our organizational strength. We are proud to be an affirmative action employer, committed to diversity, equity and inclusion of ALL people in our hiring and employment practices. We encourage applications from people who have non-dominant identities based on race, ethnicity, migration status, ability, age, gender identity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic class, etc.*

title: Medical coordinator (F/M) - Sudan
body:
For more than 40 years, Médecins du Monde (MdM), a campaigning medical organisation committed to international solidarity, has been caring for the most vulnerable populations here and abroad. It has continued to bear witness to obstacles that exist in accessing healthcare and has secured sustainable improvements in health-for-all policies.

Those working for this independent organisation do not solely dispense care and treatment but condemn violations of human dignity and rights and fight to improve matters for populations living in precarious situations.

MdM France currently works in 30 countries across all continents to facilitate access to healthcare through 6 political battles:

- Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights
- Migration, Exile, Human Rights and Health
- Harm Reduction
- Environment and Health
- Humanitarian Space
- Healthcare systems and rights

**MdM in Sudan**

MdM maintained a presence in Jebel Marra until 2011. Mid-December 2025, MdM decided to launch an exploratory mission in West Darfur and allocated core funds to provide medicines, recruit an exploratory team composed of a head of mission, a medical coordinator and a logistics coordinator, and start activities in Darfur.

Since end of April 2026, MdM is managing a clinic in the Dar Omo camp in Feina (South Darfur) hosting approximately 25.000 displaced persons.

Since August 2026, 2 mobile clinics are operating around Feina and mid-September 2026, MdM has launched a response to a cholera outbreak in North Darfur.

MdM France has decided to register itself and consolidate its presence in East Sudan to have a balanced presence in all Sudan and be able to answer humanitarian needs in this part of the country.

**About the role**

You are in charge of designing, planning, implementing, adapting and monitoring health activities. You directly manage the medical team.

**What you’ll do**

- Participate in the definition of the country strategy led by the general coordinator and drive the medical and technical aspects in the development of this strategy
- Design, plan, implement, adapt and monitor the programme’s health activities
- Ensure the quality and relevance of health activities, supervise the collection and analysis of medical data
- Recruit, manage, train, and motivate the medical team
- Ensure the management of pharmaceutical products
- Carry out health needs assessments and evaluations of medical partners
- Monitor, analyse and share health and epidemiological data and assess needs and contribute to medical response planning and emergency preparedness for epidemics and mass displacement
- Cooperate with the administration team regarding budgeting and supervise the medical purchase process
- Represent MdM with authorities, partners and other NGOs on health issues
- Participate in the writing of proposals and reports

**Who you’ll work with**

You work under the supervision of the general coordinator of the mission (based in El Geneina) and in collaboration with the health advisor, the MHPSS advisor and the pharmacy officer based at HQ. You manage directly the activity manager and the pharmacy officer. In Feina, the medical team is composed of a medical team supervisor and a midwife supervisor.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Have a medical degree (medical doctor, nurse, midwife)
- Have a minimum 4 years of experience in the humanitarian sector in a similar position
- Have experience in emergency responses, outbreak management, nutrition, health assessments and medical programme start-up
- Demonstrate experience working in complex, politically sensitive or rapidly evolving environments
- Are able to work in high security context
- Have solid background in team leadership, capacity building and technical supervision
- Have strong communication, negotiation and diplomacy skills
- Have strong ability to work collaboratively with diverse teams and multicultural stakeholders
- Have excellent organisational and time-management skills
- Have mapping skills with Google Earth or ArcGIS
- Have strong proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
- Are fluent in English (spoken and written); knowledge of Arabic is an asset

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Are not aligned with MdM’s values
- Don't have experience in volatile security environments

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

Contract & status:

- Gross monthly salary: 3 663 €
- Fixed-term contract starting as soon as possible and for 6 months
- Single posting

Work environment:

- Position based in El Geneina , West Darfur, with regular field visits

Benefits:

- 13th month salary (paid in 2 installments after 6 months of service)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

Essentials:

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumondeh.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumondeh.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know

title: Mission France - Responsable des activités de travail social F/H
body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Responsable des activités de travail social pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et l’Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution

**Votre rôle :**

Sous la responsabilité du·de la Référent·e migration, et en lien fonctionnel avec la personne responsable de la protection de l’unité migrations, vous concevrez, superviserez et suivrez les activités de travail social du projet. Vous encadrerez les travailleur·ses sociaux·les, contribuerez à la stratégie de protection et veillerez à la qualité des accompagnements proposés.

Ce poste associe pilotage stratégique, management d’équipe et intervention directe sur le terrain : vous consacrerez notamment 30 % de votre temps aux activités de travail social, aux maraudes et à l’« aller-vers ».

**Principales responsabilités :**

Piloter Définir et piloter la stratégie de travail social et de protection

- Co-définir et mettre en œuvre la stratégie de travail social du projet, en cohérence avec les orientations opérationnelles et le cadre de travail social de MSF.
- Développer les activités autour de la gestion de cas, du soutien social aux patient·es, du lien social de première ligne et des interventions communautaires.
- Analyser le contexte et les déterminants sociaux de la santé afin d’identifier les vulnérabilités récurrentes, les situations de violence, les phénomènes de déplacement et d’exclusion, ainsi que les besoins critiques d’assistance et de protection.
- Contribuer à la définition des objectifs et des interventions de protection, notamment en matière de signalement et de prévention des risques.
- Documenter les restrictions d’accès aux services et analyser les obstacles rencontrés afin de proposer des pistes d’action et de plaidoyer en lien avec la référente médicale en migration et la mission MSF France.

**Garantir un accompagnement social de qualité et gérer les situations complexes**

- Superviser les parcours d’accompagnement social : accueil, évaluation des besoins, élaboration et mise en œuvre du plan d’intervention, orientation sécurisée, suivi et clôture des situations.
- Veiller à la prise en charge des besoins sociaux critiques, dans le périmètre du projet, par un accompagnement direct ou une orientation vers des services adaptés.
- Accompagner les équipes dans la gestion des situations complexes et intervenir directement dans les cas sensibles, notamment lorsqu’il existe des risques élevés de violence ou qu’un mineur non accompagné est concerné.
- Organiser des temps réguliers de concertation autour des situations suivies, afin de partager les difficultés et de construire des réponses adaptées avec les autres disciplines.
- Favoriser le pouvoir d’agir des personnes accompagnées en leur donnant une information claire sur leurs droits, les services disponibles, les critères d’accès et les démarches pertinentes.
- Contribuer à un environnement de soins sûr, digne et confidentiel, qui respecte les droits des patient·es et facilite l’accès aux mécanismes de retours et de plaintes.

**Développer le travail social communautaire et les partenariats**

- Participer aux maraudes et aux activités d’« aller-vers » pour identifier les besoins sociaux, les vulnérabilités et les risques de protection au sein des communautés.
- Développer, avec les équipes médicales, de santé mentale et de médiation, des interventions pluridisciplinaires visant à renforcer les facteurs de protection et de résilience.
- Construire et actualiser une cartographie des services sociaux, des associations, des partenaires institutionnels et des dispositifs communautaires présents sur la zone du projet.
- Développer des relations de coopération avec les partenaires et suivre l’accessibilité, la disponibilité et la qualité des services proposés.
- Renforcer la coordination et l’orientation des personnes vers les dispositifs adaptés, en portant une attention particulière aux situations de violence, notamment sexuelle, et aux possibilités de prise en charge.
- Contribuer à la surveillance communautaire et à l’analyse des problématiques de protection rencontrées sur le terrain.

**Manager, accompagner et développer l’équipe**

- Encadrer les travailleur·ses sociaux·les et organiser les plannings en fonction des différentes activités : maraudes, entretiens individuels et activités collectives.
- Développer les compétences de l’équipe par la formation, le coaching, la supervision et le partage de pratiques.
- Identifier les besoins de développement professionnel et mettre en œuvre un plan de développement des compétences, en lien avec le département des ressources humaines.
- Former et sensibiliser les équipes aux questions de protection, de gestion de cas, de conduite d’entretien et d’orientation.
- Contribuer aux processus de recrutement, de formation et d’évaluation des équipes concernées, en collaboration avec les RH.
- Assurer la continuité des activités en apportant un soutien opérationnel et, si nécessaire, en remplaçant les membres de l’équipe absents.
- Veiller au bien-être de l’équipe et favoriser une coopération étroite avec les autres pôles du projet.

**Assurer Suivre les activités, analyser les données et garantir la qualité**

- Superviser la collecte, l’enregistrement et l’analyse des données relatives aux activités de travail social et de protection.
- Suivre les indicateurs de résultats et produire un reporting régulier permettant d’identifier les tendances, les besoins émergents et les difficultés d’accès aux services.
- Documenter les situations et les tendances en matière de protection afin d’alimenter l’analyse opérationnelle et les actions de plaidoyer de MSF.
- Développer et adapter les outils et processus de travail social aux besoins du projet.
- Garantir le respect du cadre de travail social de MSF, des règles de confidentialité, de la protection des données et des exigences légales et éthiques.
- Planifier et coordonner les ressources humaines, matérielles et financières nécessaires aux activités, en lien avec les départements support.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Diplôme français ou étranger de travailleur·se social·e, avec au moins trois années de formation théorique et pratique.
- Au moins trois ans d’expérience professionnelle dans la gestion de programmes de travail social ou de domaines similaires : protection, accompagnement psychosocial, violences sexuelles et basées sur le genre, etc.
- Expérience en gestion d’équipe.

- Sens du service et approche centrée sur la personne.

**Langues et outils :**

title: Procurement Manager, Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Procurement
body:
**Background**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to humanitarian crises in over 40 countries and in communities across the United States and Europe, helping people whose lives have been shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and rebuild their futures.

Global Procurement, within the Global Supply Chain function, leads sourcing strategy, category management, and supplier management for the organization. As IRC continues to test and adopt new technology to support its mission, Global Procurement is establishing a dedicated Procurement Manager role to provide procurement capacity for emerging technology and digital innovation.

**Position Overview**

The Procurement Manager, Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Procurement supports fast-moving technology sourcing needs across IRC, with a focus on early-stage digital innovation, pilots, proofs of concept, trials, and emerging tools. The role helps teams test and evaluate new technology quickly while maintaining procurement discipline, vendor due diligence, risk review, documentation, and compliance.

For this role, “digital innovation” refers to early-stage, small-scale, fast-moving technology initiatives where IRC teams are testing a new idea, tool, platform, vendor, or digital approach before deciding whether to scale. The portfolio covers AI and generative AI tools where applicable, SaaS and digital platforms, automation, data and analytics, migration and testing tools, cybersecurity tools, collaboration platforms, digital service delivery tools, field and mobile technology, low-code and no-code platforms, and other emerging digital solutions.

This role is an execution-focused, hands-on individual contributor role. It enables IRC to move quickly on emerging technology and digital innovation requests without bypassing procurement controls, vendor due diligence, information security, data protection, legal review, donor compliance, or documentation requirements. The Procurement Manager serves as the day-to-day procurement focal point for these requests

**Key Responsibilities**

**A. Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Sourcing Execution**

- Provide hands-on sourcing support for pilots, trials, proofs of concept, small-scale SaaS, emerging vendors, startup-style tools, and digital innovation requests across IRC.
- Execute sourcing activities in line with the IT category strategy and under the guidance of the Senior Category Manager, IT.
- Conduct early market scans and market intelligence for emerging tools, vendors, pricing models, and digital innovation categories.
- Support requirements gathering, supplier identification, RFI/RFQ/RFP preparation, evaluation support, award recommendation, and contract finalization.
- Build supplier visibility for innovation and emerging technology vendors, including startup and niche providers that may later become larger enterprise solutions.
- Help bring new tools into proper procurement channels, reducing shadow IT, credit-card purchasing, and unmanaged technology spend.
- Support SaaS rationalization, renewal planning, demand management, and license optimization at the innovation and pilot tier.
- Help business teams translate technical needs into clear scopes of work, evaluation criteria, and vendor questions.

**B. Pilot, Trial, and Proof-of-Concept Procurement Frameworks**

- Build and maintain a lightweight, repeatable procurement pathway for pilots, trials, and proofs of concept.
- Develop checklists, decision tools, and methodology for short-term technology engagements.
- Define the minimum documentation required before a pilot, trial, or proof of concept can begin.
- Maintain clear approval checkpoints and escalation criteria so teams understand when a pilot can proceed and when it requires further review.
- Track emerging technology requests from intake through pilot, decision, and possible scale-up.
- Ensure required reviews and approvals are completed and all necessary checks are documented before tools are tested or used.
- Help document whether a pilot should end, continue, scale, or move into a formal sourcing process.
- Coordinate NDAs and pre-procurement documentation when teams need to test or evaluate multiple tools before selecting a vendor.
- Ensure pilots and trials are set up in a way that allows long-term success if IRC later moves to a larger phase or formal sourcing process.

**C. AI-Enabled and High-Risk Technology Procurement Support**

- Support sourcing for AI-enabled tools as part of the broader emerging technology portfolio, applied only when AI functionality is in scope.
- For AI-enabled tools, support the application of IRC’s AI assessment requirements, including use-case risk classification, provider/deployer determination, GenAI tool checks, and required approvals.
- Coordinate with the AI Governance and Risk Committee and AI Department Focal Points when applicable.
- Identify and escalate sourcing requests that may involve high-risk technology, AI functionality, personal information, confidential data, client-facing tools, cybersecurity concerns, or unapproved tools.
- Support procurement documentation for AI-enabled tools, including evidence of approvals, vendor assessments, risk reviews, and contract requirements.

**D. Vendor Due Diligence, Risk Review, and Documentation**

- Coordinate required vendor risk assessments (VRA) and due diligence across cybersecurity, privacy and data protection, legal, donor compliance, sanctions and ATC screening, financial viability, implementation risk, integration risk, operational support model, and vendor lock-in and exit risk.
- Coordinate with Information Security, Data Protection, Office of General Counsel, Risk and Compliance, and Finance to ensure required reviews are completed before pilots, trials, awards, or contract signature.
- Ensure procurement files are complete, audit-ready, and aligned with IRC sourcing policy and donor requirements.
- Support compliance with institutional donor requirements that may affect technology, AI, data hosting, data residency, and vendor selection.
- Track and follow up on missing documentation, approvals, vendor information, and risk reviews.

**E. Tool and Vendor Visibility**

- Maintain or support a list of emerging technology tools and vendors, indicating status (under review, in pilot, approved, rejected, expired) and the approved use case for each tool.
- Document the business owner, contract status, contract dates, and renewal timing for each tool.
- Document what each tool is approved for and what use would require additional approval or new procurement action.
- Help connect business owners, end users, IT, Procurement, Information Security, Data Protection, Legal, and Finance around emerging technology tools and vendors.
- Reduce situations where approved tools are used in non-approved ways, and flag misuse for review.

**F. Contracting and Commercial Support**

- Support commercial negotiation and contracting across the emerging technology portfolio, including NDAs, trial agreements, pilot agreements, proof-of-concept agreements, SaaS agreements, subscriptions, software licenses, cloud services, implementation services, and renewals.
- Review pricing models, including seat-based licensing, usage-based pricing, token usage, API calls, implementation fees, renewal escalators, and support fees, and provide commercial analysis.
- Coordinate with Legal, IT, Finance, and business owners to ensure contracts include appropriate terms on data protection, confidentiality, intellectual property, service levels, audit rights, incident reporting, termination, data return, and exit provisions.
- For AI-enabled tools, ensure contracts also address AI-generated outputs, model training restrictions, and AI-specific risk allocation.
- Support renewal planning and help prevent last-minute renewals or unplanned vendor commitments.

**G. Stakeholder Engagement and Service Support**

- Provide practical, service-oriented procurement support to teams exploring new tools, pilots, digital services, automation platforms, AI solutions, or other emerging technology.
- Help stakeholders move through the procurement process without unnecessary delays, while maintaining compliance and risk controls.
- Coordinate between business owners, IT owners, Procurement, end users, Information Security, Data Protection, Legal, and Finance to ensure tool usage remains aligned with approved scope, contract terms, procurement files, risk approvals, and any applicable usage guidelines.
- Reduce workarounds, shadow IT, and credit-card purchasing by making the correct procurement process easier to follow.
- Guide stakeholders on procurement routes, required documentation, approval steps, and realistic timelines for emerging technology procurement.
- Support early engagement with teams considering new tools, pilots, or digital approaches, before commitments are made to vendors.

**H. Reporting and Continuous Improvement**

- Track the emerging technology sourcing pipeline, renewal calendar, cycle time, savings, risk flags, documentation completion, and approval status.
- Track pilot outcomes (end, continue, scale, or formal sourcing) and capture lessons learned.
- Track user adoption issues, non-approved usage of approved tools, and other compliance signals, and surface these to the Senior Category Manager, IT.
- Identify recurring issues in emerging technology sourcing and recommend improvements to frameworks, checklists, templates, and decision tools.
- Contribute to knowledge sharing across Global Procurement on emerging technology, SaaS, AI, and digital innovation sourcing practices.
- Support the role’s value contribution by improving visibility over fast-moving technology spend, reducing duplicated tools, undocumented pilots, and audit risk.

**Key Working Relationships**

- **Reports to:** Senior Category Manager, IT.
- **Internal:** Office of the CIO and IT teams; Senior Category Manager, IT; Information Security; Data Protection; Office of General Counsel; Ethics and Compliance; Risk and Compliance; Finance; Airbel Impact Lab; Data and Analytics; External Relations; Country Program supply chain and innovation leads; program innovation teams; fundraising and digital teams; AI Governance and Risk Committee when applicable; Global Procurement peers.
- **External:** Emerging technology vendors and resellers; SaaS, cloud, cybersecurity, automation, data, and AI providers; startup and niche technology vendors; industry analysts; peer humanitarian and development organizations.

**Minimum Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in procurement, supply chain, business administration, information technology, engineering, law, or a related field. Equivalent experience may be considered.
- Minimum 5 to 7 years of procurement, sourcing, contract management, or vendor management experience.
- Of the required 5 to 7 years above, at least 3 years must be in IT procurement, SaaS and software sourcing, software licensing, cloud services, cybersecurity tools, data platforms, or similar technology categories.
- Experience supporting pilots, trials, proofs of concept, or other early-stage technology procurement activities.
- Experience coordinating vendor due diligence and technology risk reviews, including cybersecurity, data protection, financial, and operational risk.
- Experience supporting sourcing events, supplier evaluations, commercial analysis, and contract coordination.
- Good understanding of technology procurement risks, including data protection, information security, intellectual property, software licensing, vendor lock-in, and third-party risk.
- Ability to work effectively with IT, Legal, Information Security, Data Protection, Finance, and business teams.
- Demonstrated ability to work quickly while maintaining compliance, controls, and documentation standards.
- Strong stakeholder service orientation and ability to balance procurement standards with customer needs.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Good judgment and ability to balance speed, compliance, risk, and stakeholder needs.
- Experience in an NGO, donor-funded organization, humanitarian agency, UN agency, or complex global organization.
- Knowledge of donor compliance requirements such as USAID/BHA, FCDO, ECHO, EU, UN agencies, or private foundations.
- Professional certification such as CIPS, CPSM, or equivalent, completed or in progress.
- Working knowledge of French, Spanish, or Arabic is an advantage.

**Working Environment**

Flexible (IRC hub city preferred; remote considered). Travel of up to 10% domestically and internationally, including occasional travel to IRC country offices.

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Lebanon, Germany, Kenya, Pakistan, and Jordan.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Strategy and Planning Senior Officer, Global Policy & Advocacy
body:
**Background**: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people affected by humanitarian crises to survive, recover and rebuild their lives. We deliver lasting impact by providing health care, helping children learn, and empowering individuals and communities to become self-reliant, always with a focus on the unique needs of women and girls. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, we now work in over 40 crisis-affected countries as well as communities throughout the U.S., Europe and Latin America.

The External Relations (ER) Department mobilizes external audiences to raise the requisite funds, influence policies and achieve practice changes to improve outcomes for our clients, while growing and protecting our global brand. The Global Policy & Advocacy team is a dynamic part of the ER Department that leverages the power of IRC’s ideas to solve the biggest challenges facing IRC’s clients across the “arc of crisis” and influence external stakeholders, in particular governments and multi-lateral institutions, to enact these solutions to ultimately make meaningful change for our clients. From addressing the drivers of conflict to meeting the needs of displaced people, the team partners with innovative thinkers, experts and those with lived experience to identify solutions and bring them to life. We take pride in being solutions-oriented and creative. We are precise in our goals, tactics, and messages. We drive change year over year, knowing that system change takes dedicated focus while maintaining the flexibility to respond to emerging needs across the globe. Finally, we are collaborative, constantly seeking new ideas and perspectives from others in our sector and beyond as we work side by side with programs, strategy, communications and research and innovation teams across the IRC.

**Job Overview/Summary:**

The Strategy and Planning Senior Officer will lead on key strategic planning and prioritization efforts for the Policy & Advocacy team. The Senior Officer will coordinate portions of organization-wide strategy and investment planning, collaborate with the Vice President of Policy & Advocacy on team prioritization processes, and manage a collaborative but streamlined process for strategy development. This person will maintain crucial processes and relationships and collaborate at all levels within and across the teams, and across the IRC.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- **Facilitate priority-setting processes:** Translate organization-wide strategy and policy products into department strategies, market-specific advocacy priorities, and thematic policy areas of focus.
- **Lead strategy development processes:** Work closely with Policy and Advocacy team members to support the development of specific, actionable policy and advocacy strategies, helping individual units develop strategies relevant to their priority issues and their geographic/political markets that include stakeholder mapping, activity planning, product development plans, and desired external change metrics as relevant. Lead Policy and Advocacy engagement in organization-wide annual planning processes, linking Policy and Advocacy planning to multi-year organizational strategies and Department-wide objectives.
- **Develop and facilitate activities and processes across Policy and Advocacy teams:** Facilitate and maintain efficient ways of working within, across, and with the Policy and Advocacy teams as appropriate. Identify and elevate collaboration challenges and develop ways of working systems to address those issues. Ensure ways of working are routinely updated to address feedback from team members and represent team in org-wide, multi-departmental process conversations.
- **Manage long-term projects**: Own project management, strategic content development, and logistics for key team efforts such as the Annual Planning and Quarterly Pause processes, retreat planning, and others.
- **Facilitate cross-team collaboration and communication:** Create tools and processes for effectively sharing information and collaborating internally, communicating with IRC stakeholders routinely, and managing workflows in a streamlined and smooth manner. Facilitate regular, effective, and efficient communication between team members and from organizational leadership to the rest of the teams, cascading information from ER leadership, finance, and HR as necessary. Manage the internal website and routine reporting to senior leaders. Develop deep understanding of Policy and Advocacy priorities and strategies in order to communicate effectively about team objectives and outcomes with internal stakeholders through reporting processes, internal websites, email and other means as appropriate.
- **Lead KPI development and progress tracking:** Working with the VP and members of the Policy and Advocacy team develop a set of high-level objectives for teams alongside a more detailed set of KPIs to enable reporting out to the organization on progress. Plan and facilitate quarterly internal progress reviews of individual strategies (and associated metrics) across Policy and Advocacy. Ensure KPIs and reporting metrics are logical, consistent, and regularly reported on by team members on a weekly basis.
- **Teamwork:** Support a positive team culture by acting openly and collaboratively, supporting colleagues in their work and sharing credit with others where appropriate. Organize team retreats, staff meetings, team building activities and trainings.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Vice President of Policy & Advocacy with a Management in Partnership to the Director of Strategy & Planning  
**Position directly supervises:** N/A  
**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal:*** Global Policy and Advocacy team; Strategy & Planning Team; Business Operations; Marketing and Mobilization; Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department; Resettlement, Asylum and Integration Department; President’s Office; Finance; Information Technology; Human Resources

***External:*** NGOs, think tanks, U.S. government agencies, Congress, multilateral institutions and other organizations as needed

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:*** Bachelor’s degree in International Relations, Political Science or other related field

***Work Experience:***

- 5-6 years work experience, experience in policy and advocacy preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Excellent organizational and time management skills, including juggling competing priorities and tight deadlines and prioritizing tasks appropriately
- Experience designing and implementing strategic planning processes and progress metrics
- Positive, resourceful and flexible attitude with ability to problem solve, work productively both in a team environment or independently as needed, and take initiative in a fast-faced environment
- Familiarity with or experience in policy analysis or advocacy to high-level policymakers and thought leaders
- Strong project management skills, ideally within a cross-organizational team to deliver on projects/strategies
- Solid English language writing and editing skills with a focus on details
- Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to develop and manage complex relationships, including with high-level individuals
- Familiarity with or proven interest in humanitarian aid sector, foreign policy, and/or refugee issues
- Fluency in Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and ability to learn online web-based applications
- Ambition to learn and grow skills by taking on challenging tasks, and mastering complex content and concepts
- Commitment to advancing equity, diversity, and inclusion at the IRC and in the humanitarian field
- Lived experience with conflict or crisis-driven displacement, resettlement, asylum, immigration or migration is an asset in this role

\*\*Working Environment:\*\*Hybrid office work environment. Up to 5% travel may be required.

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United States of America.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $92,000 - $99,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.
